stories.Headline: Microsoft closes 1,413 vulnerabilities and accelerates patching with AI
stories.Summary:
Microsoft has detailed its security strategy after closing 1,413 vulnerabilities during its October 2026 update cycle. Of those, 1,123 affected Windows, compared with 134 the previous year, a rise of 738 percent. The company credits much of this pace to MDASH, an agentic scanning system that relies on more than one hundred AI agents working alongside several language models. Those agents analyze code, classify risks, and filter out duplicate reports.

MDASH combines its agents to scan code for flaws, assign risk levels, and remove duplicate reports before they reach engineers. In testing, the system reached a recall of one hundred percent on seven flaws in tcpip.sys and 88.45 percent on the CyberGym benchmark. Final validation still rests with human engineers. For development and system administration teams, the change means vulnerability management becomes faster and more automated. It also means that updates must be applied without delay and that CSAF and VEX data should be consumed programmatically.

Microsoft warns that the same AI capabilities speed up attackers, and it advises against postponing patch installation. The company's message is that flaws are now being found far more quickly, so waiting to deploy fixes carries greater risk. Administrators who still delay updates until a convenient moment are being told that this habit no longer fits the current threat pace. The articles do not describe any specific attack that has exploited these flaws.

Articles.Title: Microsoft closes 1,413 vulnerabilities and accelerates patching with AI

stories.Headline: A US host's 24 hours in Wuzhen: How AI goes to work
stories.Summary:
From November 2 to 5, 2026, the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit is being held in Wuzhen, a water town in Jiaxing, Zhejiang province in East China. It is the 13th time the summit has met there. This year, organizers want to show a different side of artificial intelligence, which they say is no longer just an exhibit but has already started working in everyday settings. A host from the United States, named Jeremy, attended the first conference in 2014 and has returned twelve years later. He finds the town now full of self-driving vehicles where a ride-hailing app once impressed him.

The shift reflects a broader change in which humanoid robots are moving from laboratory prototypes to factory products. Shipments in China are expected to reach 62,500 units in 2026. At the "Light of the Internet" Expo and the AI Carnival, embodied-AI robots are working in real settings such as factories, hotels, hospitals and homes. The reporting presents these demonstrations as evidence that the technology is now being used in practice rather than only displayed. The articles give no further figures on costs or adoption rates.

Walking through the town, Jeremy sees AI built into daily routines. In the 5G smart greenhouse at Zhengfu village, tomato farmers rely on data rather than the weather to guide their work. On the streets, self-driving vehicles slow down for children at play, braking, stopping and steering around them. Robot guide dogs lead visually impaired pedestrians across zebra crossings. Elsewhere, robot dogs take on repetitive and hazardous tasks at zero-carbon factories and at the 110 kV Chenzhuang substation.

In an elderly care center, one robot rests its head beside a resident's hand without making a sound, simply keeping them company. The articles close by asking whether AI will replace people or open a wider world, and they leave that judgment to each observer. They name the China Daily as the source of the report, and the conference itself is organized under the World Internet Conference framework. The articles do not say who ultimately sets policy for these deployments or what outcomes the summit will produce.

Articles.Title: A US host's 24 hours in Wuzhen: How AI goes to work - China Daily

stories.Headline: E-Town ramps up AI tokens thrust
stories.Summary:
Beijing's Economic-Technological Development Area, known as E-Town, is building an AI ecosystem around what it calls a token economy, and it showed its plans at the ongoing 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The exhibit, a 12-square-meter display, featured the area's efforts in space-based computing, semiconductors, infrastructure, large models and application platforms. The centerpiece is Beijing's first token factory, recently completed in the development area, which has nearly 10,000 petaflops of computing capacity. Unlike conventional data centers that mainly rent out computing resources, the token factory combines hardware, AI inference software and model optimization to deliver standardized AI processing services.

E-Town is also planning a distribution platform that would give developers access to different AI models and computing systems through one unified interface, with requests routed according to their needs. The aim is to connect large-scale token production with demand from companies and developers. Tokens, the basic data units AI models use to process and generate information, are increasingly used to measure AI workloads and price AI services. In August, the area introduced trial measures to support a token-driven intelligent economy. By 2030 it aims to establish four token factories, each with at least 10,000 accelerator cards, and to build an intelligent economy worth more than 400 billion yuan, or about $60 billion.

The showcase also included partner companies' technologies. Houmo.AI presented its M50 chip, an energy-efficient edge AI processor designed for large-model inference, intended to support AI deployment closer to end users and devices. ZTE Corp displayed its OEX orthogonal backplane-free interconnect architecture for supercomputing clusters, which is compatible with mainstream graphics processing units and has already entered commercial use among leading internet companies, telecom operators and government and corporate clients. VAST demonstrated Tripo P2.0, a 3D foundation model that generates structured 3D assets meeting industrial production standards within seconds. Maimai Technology Group showed agricultural robots powered by embodied intelligence.

The token economy reflects growing demand for AI inference. According to data from the National Data Administration, China's average daily token calls exceeded 500 trillion by June, up from 100 billion in early 2024. The strategy marks a shift from developing individual AI technologies toward building a coordinated industrial chain, in which advances in hardware and computing infrastructure support model development while practical applications generate demand for further improvements. The articles do not say how the planned distribution platform will be launched or when the 2030 targets will be reviewed.

Articles.Title: E-Town ramps up AI tokens thrust - China Daily

stories.Headline: Gao Zhikai: International cooperation can advance global AI development
stories.Summary:
Gao Zhikai, vice-president of the Center for China and Globalization, said in an interview during the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit that artificial intelligence and the internet should promote progress and serve the public good. The interview was published by China Daily on November 7, 2026. He made these remarks at the event in Wuzhen, where the summit took place. The articles present his comments as a call for broader international cooperation in the field.

Gao argued that as AI develops rapidly, it is important to think about how to better protect the continuity of the different civilizations, cultures and traditions found across countries. He called for international cooperation in AI to help countries around the world advance their AI development steadily. In his view, the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen offers a prime platform where AI and internet development can support and reinforce each other. The articles report his views as his own and do not describe any formal commitment, agreement or new requirement.

Gao holds the post of vice-president at the Center for China and Globalization, and the articles attribute these views to him in that role. The piece is a short interview, and the articles give no further detail on specific measures, timelines or figures tied to his proposals. The China Daily summary notes that it was generated by AI and that the publication takes no responsibility for it, so readers should rely on the interview text itself. The same page lists other unrelated items, including an exhibition on Yunnan and a discussion of AI and jobs, but the articles do not connect them to Gao's remarks. The articles do not say what follow-up steps, if any, are planned.

Articles.Title: Gao Zhikai: International cooperation can advance global AI development - China Daily

stories.Headline: Nvidia Takes Physical AI to the Auto Market First, Giving Away Models Free to Capture Compute Revenue
stories.Summary:
Nvidia has moved to give away its physical AI models, including the Cosmos world foundation model and the Alpamayo autonomous-driving model, to automakers for free. The strategy is reported in a November 8, 2026 finance article covering the company's automotive business. Nvidia's automotive segment revenue reached $2.349 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended January 25, 2026, up 39% year over year. The company's China team is also working on cost reductions for automakers and developers.

The changes described in the articles center on cutting cost and development time. Nvidia's China engineers built a lightweight inference framework that, combined with FP4 quantization, helps some automakers cut intelligent-driving domain controller memory from 32GB to 16GB. The company also modified its middleware so that the main chip's vision accelerator can process raw millimeter-wave radar signals, removing the need for a separate radar chip. Nvidia has expanded its definition of automotive developers to include all companies that develop and sell their own software, including automakers and intelligent-driving suppliers. Automotive-grade memory chip prices reportedly rose about 180% from March to June 2026, which raised pressure on automakers to lower hardware costs.

Nvidia is the company pursuing this strategy, and its executives described the reasoning behind it. The company's personnel said the aim is to bring foundation models to a passing standard so that automakers need only modest compute and their own road-test data for fine-tuning. They also said that as the industry adopts the open framework, customers will use more of Nvidia's platforms, which will translate into sustained demand for cloud training and simulation compute. Wu Peidong, managing director of Wanchuang Investment Bank, was quoted as saying the open tools change the starting point rather than the finish line, and that free does not mean zero cost. The articles also say Nvidia's share of China's passenger-car assisted-driving domain control chip market fell from 45.1% in early 2026 to 30.2% in August, while Horizon Robotics and Huawei are gaining ground.

The context is a competitive market in which automakers such as NIO, XPeng and Li Auto are building in-house chips, and Chinese regulators are preparing rules for higher automation levels. China's mandatory national standard for automated driving systems, published in August 2026, is scheduled to take effect July 1, 2027, and applies to vehicles with L3 and L4 systems. Some automakers have dropped L3 systems in favor of L2++ assisted driving. The articles say Nvidia's hardware reference design targets L4 with two independent sets of power and sensors and a dual-chip primary and backup arrangement. Wu Peidong expects Nvidia to keep a share of automakers for roughly two to three years, while the company's investment focus is also shifting toward robotaxis and overseas automakers.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Takes Physical AI to the Auto Market First, Giving Away Models Free to Capture Compute Revenue

stories.Headline: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant
stories.Summary:
Yelp has adopted a hybrid user interface architecture for its AI Assistant, pairing native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering so that interface changes can roll out faster across platforms. The design relies on Yelp's CHAOS framework, which stands for Content Hosting Architecture with Optimization Strategies, to render the conversation content. Navigation and message input remain native to each app. The approach was reported by InfoQ on November 6, 2026.

The Yelp Assistant first launched on iOS in 2024 to help users create project requests for local service professionals. It has since grown to answer questions about businesses and to support actions such as reservations, appointments, and food orders. CHAOS supports web, iOS, and Android. In a server-driven model, the backend defines what the client displays and how it responds to interactions, which means interface changes can reach users without a new mobile app release. The article does not give figures for adoption or release timing beyond these points.

Yelp engineers explained that the existing CHAOS framework lacked some capabilities the Assistant needed, including text input fields and network requests. Extending the framework would have delayed delivery, so the team kept navigation and message input native and used CHAOS only for the conversation area. The implementation separates view configuration from conversation data: the client fetches the CHAOS configuration when a chat starts, and later events update the existing view without refetching it. Those events cover persistent messages, temporary typing indicators and quick replies, and links, and the backend can also send actions such as disabling chat input once a project request is complete.

Yelp's engineers also acknowledged trade-offs. The architecture brings coordination challenges, engineers needed time to learn both the Assistant and CHAOS, and shared implementations can still behave differently across platforms. The article notes that separating view configuration from conversation data allows independent feature development and that the Android Assistant was reused to launch the Biz Ask Anything pilot. According to Yelp, this work laid the groundwork for its next-generation Assistant, which connects business information with actions users can take. The article also compares the approach with Airbnb's Ghost Platform, which likewise uses server-defined UI across web and mobile clients.

Articles.Title: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant - infoq.com

stories.Headline: Ai+toolkit | Tag | techmonk
stories.Summary:
Block has launched Builderlab, an enterprise intelligence toolkit, according to a TechGig article dated November 6, 2026. The toolkit is built on Buzz, Block's open-source workspace. The article says the toolkit is meant to bring discussion and execution together in software building. It is positioned as going beyond individual AI tools.

The article gives no further details on pricing, availability, or specific features. It also does not name a launch date beyond the article's publication date. The surrounding page content is mostly unrelated event listings, including the IndiaAI Challenge 2026, Ericsson recruitment events, and DevNext 2026, and carries no further information about Builderlab. The article does not name a specific person quoted about the launch, and it does not provide any statement from Block's leadership.

Its description of the toolkit's purpose comes from the article itself rather than from a company quote. Beyond the publication, the articles offer no account of who developed the toolkit or how it is being rolled out. The articles carry too little for a full account, so this is treated as a breaking story. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Microsoft: AI Agent Took 5 Minutes From GitHub to Key Vault
stories.Summary:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence said on November 5 that, in at least one case, it observed an AI agent move from scanning GitHub for secrets to pulling data out of Azure Key Vault in five minutes. The company says threat actors have used an agentic AI offensive framework since August 2026 to search public GitHub repositories for exposed credentials and AI service keys, then use those keys against the organizations they belong to. Microsoft's post does not name the actor behind the activity. A follow-on attack that began as early as October 28 used valid leaked or stolen application credentials to sign in to Microsoft Entra ID tenants, and Microsoft says the agent successfully conducted service principal sign-ins on dozens of associated applications across multiple tenants.

Microsoft does not give a count of affected customers, referring only to "some impacted customers." The company says the agents repeatedly focused on credentials that give access to AI services, including API keys for major AI providers and OAuth applications with access to Foundry Tools, which was previously called Azure Cognitive Services. In one attack Microsoft described, the agent corrected failed cloud requests on its own: a rerun with a supported API version succeeded about 28 seconds after the first failed response, and two similar retries followed failures after about 60 and 80 seconds. Microsoft warns that blocking traffic by IP address, user agent or other fingerprints will not stop such an attack, because the agent can change them quickly.

Its guidance is to scan GitHub code for secrets, remove them and rotate any exposed keys. It also says to treat exposed credentials as compromised even if the original location has been edited or deleted. Microsoft also recommends limiting who can register applications, applying Conditional Access policies to workload identities, and enabling Defender for Cloud plans including Defender for Key Vault. It says honeypots, tarpits and "fake wins" can draw autonomous AI attacks away from real targets, and that in its testing these controls reduced attack traffic reaching real assets.

The post also lists detections in Microsoft's own Defender and Sentinel products and promotes Security Copilot agents, which Microsoft sells. Separately, Microsoft reported on October 21 that in another ARTEX campaign the time from initial targeting to privileged access was in some instances less than 3 hours. The two figures measure different steps in different campaigns, so they do not show a measured speed-up. The company's findings have not been independently verified.

Articles.Title: Microsoft: AI Agent Took 5 Minutes From GitHub to Key Vault

stories.Headline: Chip Industry Week In Review - Semiconductor Engineering
stories.Summary:
SK hynix expects memory supply constraints to persist through 2030, with DRAM and HBM volumes effectively sold out through 2029, the company said in the week’s review. Samsung expects tight memory supply through 2028, citing lengthy fab construction and equipment lead times, larger dies, and greater process complexity in next-gen HBM. Samsung also said its 2027 HBM supply is already sold out. Solidigm, SK hynix’s U.S. subsidiary, reportedly is discussing a proposed $45B NAND flash fab with the U.S. Commerce Department. China’s CXMT plans to soon begin limited production of HBM3E memory despite manufacturing yields of just 20% to 30%, per Reuters.

Anthropic warned in its IPO filing that HBM shortages and limited TSMC manufacturing capacity could constrain AI expansion. ASE forecasts a doubling of its advanced-packaging revenue in 2027, and Amkor is ramping new high-density fan-out and 2.5D packaging programs. TSMC reportedly is considering a 20% price increase for CoWoS as AI demand continues to strain advanced-packaging capacity. Applied Materials plans to increase its stake in Besi to about 20%, deepening a strategic partnership that is expanding beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and advanced packaging technologies for AI.

The review also covered manufacturing and AI tool news. Intel Foundry reported improving manufacturing execution in Q3, citing better yields and cycle times on 18A, and released its 14A 0.9 PDK in October. Infineon plans to invest €1.1B through 2034 at its Villach, Austria facility to establish Europe’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next-gen GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers. UMC approved an additional $3.2B in capital spending to accelerate capacity expansion in Singapore and Tainan. Lam Research and imec expanded their collaboration on advanced 3D integration, next-gen memory, and high-NA EUV patterning.

On the AI side, Cadence introduced a portfolio of domain-specialized AI models for agentic chip and system design, and Arm introduced a new CPU benchmarking methodology for agentic AI. Google is expanding the reach of its custom AI accelerators, with OpenAI reportedly planning to purchase its TPUs, reports The Information. Oracle will offer Google’s TPUs through its cloud infrastructure beginning in 2027 and plans to add Arm’s AGI CPUs in fall 2027. Broadcom’s XPUs and networking equipment will support Anthropic’s AI infrastructure expansion, beginning in 2027, under a $63B financing arrangement.

Articles.Title: Chip Industry Week In Review - Semiconductor Engineering

stories.Headline: [News] MediaTek Reportedly Taps Intel Packaging Veteran After TSMC Hire, Advances Dual CoWoS–EMIB Strategy
stories.Summary:
MediaTek has hired Navid Shahriari, a former Intel executive vice president, as senior vice president, with the appointment effective November 9. Reports from Liberty Times and BigGo Finance, both published in early November 2026, say he will report directly to President and Chief Operating Officer Joe Chen. The move is the company's second major advanced packaging hire this year, following its May 2026 engagement of former TSMC research and development vice president Yu Chen-hua as an advisor. Shahriari brings 37 years of experience in semiconductor design engineering and advanced packaging, along with hands-on work in the data center market.

In his new role, Shahriari will oversee teams covering advanced process and yield platforms, design-technology co-optimization, advanced testing and packaging, and quality and reliability. MediaTek has said one of his core missions is to deepen collaboration with TSMC and other key supply chain partners. The aim is to integrate advanced technologies that strengthen the company's artificial intelligence and high-performance computing products. Reports describe the appointment as part of a wider effort to move MediaTek beyond smartphone chips toward data center AI chips. Reuters reports that the company supports both TSMC's CoWoS and Intel's EMIB packaging technologies, letting customers choose between them.

Shahriari spent most of his career at Intel, where he served as executive vice president of Intel Foundry and oversaw packaging, testing, and advanced packaging strategy before retiring in June of this year. According to the reports, he led development of complex packaging and substrate technologies and supported production at several large manufacturing sites. Reports also say MediaTek has worked with Intel on its EMIB technology for certain cloud ASIC projects, including work tied to Google's TPU program. MediaTek has not publicly detailed how Shahriari's work will be measured.

The hiring comes as MediaTek ramps up its AI accelerator ASIC business. According to Focus Taiwan, the company began shipping its first AI accelerator ASIC in September 2026 and expects roughly US$2.5 billion in revenue from it in the fourth quarter. MediaTek is targeting about US$16 billion in AI ASIC revenue and a 20% market share in 2027, with its next-generation accelerator slated for commercial production in the first quarter of 2028. Analysts cited by BigGo Finance note that advanced packaging capacity remains a bottleneck across the AI supply chain. They say whether MediaTek turns its new talent into project progress will still depend on coordination with its foundry and packaging partners.

Articles.Title: [News] MediaTek Reportedly Taps Intel Packaging Veteran After TSMC Hire, Advances Dual CoWoS–EMIB Strategy - TrendForce

stories.Headline: Klleon Sees AI Humans Moving From Guides to Entertainers
stories.Summary:
Klleon, a Korean AI human technology company, is pushing its digital human technology from guidance and education into entertainment, with the shift described by Klleon's chief product officer Seo Ji-ho at the "U-KNOCK 2026 in USA" event at the Biltmore Hotel in Los Angeles on January 6. The article, published November 8, 2026 by Seoul Economic Daily, reports that AI is moving from one-way content toward real-time conversation shaped by a user's questions and responses. Klleon's technology is now used mainly in business-to-business and business-to-government projects, where AI humans act as guides in public institutions and retail spaces. The company also offers role-playing training for sales and customer service staff, along with products such as Klleon Studio, an SDK for embedding real-time avatars in other services, and RollFit, a training solution that lets managers set scenarios.

Klleon is also expanding into entertainment, supplying AI human technology to "My AI Partner," an SBS variety program released through Netflix in August that has broadcasters interact with AI humans over a set period. Seo said emotional exchange will matter more in entertainment than the information delivery that defined guidance and education. He added that the technology could expand into entertainment and business-to-consumer content. The company's visit to the United States was meant to gauge how local consumers respond to AI content, and it found that some saw AI as a tool to extend creators' imagination while others felt AI output lacks a human touch. Seo said he had come to see those cultural differences for himself, noting that fear and resistance toward AI appeared stronger in the U.S. than in Korea or Asia.

According to Seo, companies should not rush to seize the market but should understand cultural and national differences and prepare technology that fits human expression. The article frames the key to Klleon's expansion as whether AI humans can establish themselves as technology that communicates with people rather than replaces them. Klleon plans to broaden its market by advancing the technology and increasing content uses that reflect each country's cultural traits. The article does not give further figures, timelines or results for these plans.

Articles.Title: Klleon Sees AI Humans Moving From Guides to Entertainers - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea to Gather 100 Citizens to Debate AI Fake News Rules
stories.Summary:
South Korea's government will convene a panel of 100 citizens to discuss how to respond to fake news generated by artificial intelligence, with the aim of shaping future AI policy around the views collected. The Ministry of Science and ICT and the National AI Strategy Committee will hold the first Public Deliberation Forum on AI Issues in Seoul on the 12th, and the agencies announced the plan on the 7th. The 100 participants are to be selected to represent a cross-section of the public. The government says the forum will examine the many ways AI affects democracy and discuss the direction society should take.

The first topic is AI-generated fake news. As regulators weigh changes, including widening the range of deepfake material that must carry a mandatory AI label, the forum will take up where freedom of expression should end and regulation should begin. Participants will look at gray-area content, such as realistic satirical videos featuring real people and synthetic material with no sign it was made with AI. Under the current AI Framework Act, deepfakes must carry a notice that they were made with AI, though creative works may display the label in a way that does not disrupt viewing. The government launched a public participation platform called Modu AI late last month to support the effort.

The government also plans to discuss how much responsibility AI developers and content distribution platforms should bear. Under current law, the duty to disclose AI-made deepfakes falls only on AI businesses. To reduce industry confusion, the government has suspended fines for violations until at least January 22 next year. President Lee Jae-myung has separately called for a stronger response to fake news in general. At a Cabinet meeting on the 3rd, he said incitement driven by fake news is becoming a highly effective tool and causes social harm that requires a strong response.

Articles.Title: Korea to Gather 100 Citizens to Debate AI Fake News Rules - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: AI-Driven Quantification of Coronary Plaque Outperforms Standard Care in Suspected CAD
stories.Summary:
A randomized trial called PARAMOUNT, presented at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago, found that an AI-based coronary CT analysis outperformed standard care for patients with suspected coronary artery disease. The study, led by Todd Villines, MD, of the University of Virginia, compared a plaque-based management strategy with usual care. Villines discussed the findings in an interview with HCPLive, and the results were described as preliminary. The trial enrolled 530 patients at 21 sites between January 2025 and February 2026.

The trial enrolled symptomatic adults older than 18 who were suspected of having coronary artery disease, excluding those with an LDL below 100 mg/dL, those already treated beyond primary prevention guidelines, and those with suspected acute coronary syndrome. Patients were randomly assigned to either coronary plaque-based care or usual care. The plaque-based group underwent coronary CT angiography with AI-enabled assessment of plaque morphology and composition. The primary endpoint combined several measures, including diagnostic certainty, LDL reduction, and avoidance of unnecessary invasive angiography and stenting.

Among the enrolled patients, the median age was 57 years, 57% were women, and the median baseline LDL-C was 128 mg/dL. At 180 days, plaque-based care was favorable to standard care, with a win ratio of 2 (95% CI, 1.37-2.56; P less than .0001). Diagnostic certainty about the presence of coronary artery disease contributed most to the primary endpoint. The investigators concluded that AI-based plaque assessment may give physicians greater confidence when evaluating chest pain.

Villines noted that the speed and standardization of AI-generated reports should continue to improve as coronary CT scan volumes grow. He said AI could help reading physicians with pre-reads and plaque staging, making their work more efficient. Full results are expected in early 2027. Villines reported consulting for Cleerly, HeartFlow, and Milestone.

Articles.Title: AI-Driven Quantification of Coronary Plaque Outperforms Standard Care in Suspected CAD

stories.Headline: TSMC Stock And 2 AI Infrastructure Shares Riding The AGI Spending Wave
stories.Summary:
The article is a Yahoo Finance roundup built around the headline "TSMC Stock And 2 AI Infrastructure Shares Riding The AGI Spending Wave," published November 7, 2026. It is a Simply Wall St style piece that points to recent spending plans from Meta, OpenAI partners and Anthropic, which it says are sending billions into chips, cloud and power. The author argues that this capital flow can lift some stocks while squeezing others that misjudge demand or pricing. The piece profiles three companies, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Tokyo Electron and ASML Holding, as exposed to that spending.

The article describes Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing as turning hyperscaler AI spending into chips for datacenters, phones and cars. It names the company's advanced logic demand as a driver, saying it scales with compute complexity rather than unit volume. The piece says the key question is how a growing tension around future AI capacity will affect pricing power and margins. It also describes Tokyo Electron as a supplier whose production tools sit in fabs building AI chips, and it cites the ramp of the Miyagi Innovative Production Center, which management indicates could triple production capacity.

ASML Holding is presented as a bottleneck stock because its lithography tools are required for advanced chips, and the article notes export restrictions involving China have made it a geopolitical chokepoint. The article does not name a specific person as responsible for the analysis, and the commentary is attributed to Simply Wall St and written with AI assistance. It states that the content is general in nature, is based on historical data and analyst forecasts, and is not financial advice or a recommendation to buy or sell any stock. The author of the page is listed as Bailey Pemberton.

The piece also notes that it may not factor in the latest price-sensitive company announcements. The article offers links to a wider screen of 136 more AI infrastructure companies and to other curated stock lists. The article does not describe any specific outcome or next step beyond the general expectation that the spending wave will keep shaping pricing, capacity and margins across these suppliers. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Artificial intelligence (AI) is determining the fate of the two giants in the global advertising mar..
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms and Google are facing diverging fortunes in the global advertising market as artificial intelligence reshapes the industry. According to CNBC, Meta's advertising revenue in the third quarter of this year reached $63.1 billion, up 26% from $50.1 billion a year earlier. Google's search revenue over the same period grew only 12% to $63.4 billion, and the gap between the two growth rates was 14 percentage points, the widest in Meta's favor since 2021. Google also earned an additional $11 billion from YouTube in the quarter.

Meta's rebound followed a difficult stretch after Apple tightened its privacy policies in 2021, which hurt personalized advertising, and Meta's annual revenue fell for the first time in its history the following year. The company then pushed AI into its ad business, and its Meta AI Business Assistant, launched last year, helps advertisers build campaigns and improve performance. Meta's chief financial officer, Susan Li, said advertisers using AI recommendations saw conversion rates about 5% higher and raised their ad spending by 9%. About 10 million advertisers used Meta's AI advertising tools in the third quarter, and one food company reported a 57% rise in purchases and a 36% drop in advertising cost per purchase.

Google faces a different problem, as consumers using AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude click through to websites less often, weakening the traffic that search advertising depends on. Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, which summarize search results with AI, have also raised concerns about further erosion of search ad revenue. Although Google reported record search volume in the third quarter, growth in its search division slowed, and the investment bank UBS said the threat from chatbots was again raising doubts about the search business. Both companies are spending heavily to keep pace, with Google forecasting up to $205 billion in capital expenditure this year and Meta up to $145 billion, a combined $350 billion, while free cash flow at both has turned negative.

The two companies differ in how exposed they are. Google has expanded its cloud business so that advertising now accounts for less than two-thirds of its total revenue, whereas Meta still relies on advertising for 98% of its revenue. The investment bank Wedbush said Google's share price would likely recover only if investors' view of its search business changes, and that evidence is needed that search advertising can still produce revenue in the AI era as it did before. Whether the massive AI spending will pay off for either company remains unresolved.

Articles.Title: Artificial intelligence (AI) is determining the fate of the two giants in the global advertising mar..

stories.Headline: 10 Best Black Friday AI Gadget Deals in 2026: Top Picks
stories.Summary:
Black Friday AI gadget deals are being tracked ahead of November 27, 2026, with Cyber Monday following on November 30. Memeburn published a guide on November 8, 2026, comparing ten gadgets on price history and running costs. The article says the discounts it tracks come from October's Prime Big Deal Days and last year's sales, and that October already set the price floors. The guide notes that retailers often start promotions before the main shopping weekend, so early discounts may appear throughout November.

The article gives several floors and targets. The AirPods Pro 3 fell from $249 to $179 during Amazon's October 6 to 7 Prime event, and the article says MacRumors has tracked $169 as its all-time low. The Echo Dot Max dropped to $79.99 in December and again during Prime Big Deal Days, after launching at $99 and later rising to $119.99. The Pixel Watch 5 sits at $299 for the 41mm model at many retailers, and the article says a price below that would make it more interesting.

Several products carry ongoing costs, including the Oura membership at $69.99 a year and the Plaud Pro plan at $99.99 a year. The article is written by Michael Sacchitello and was last updated on November 8, 2026. It says the author compared official specifications, manufacturer prices, retailer listings, and independent reviews. It also states that official Black Friday prices have not been confirmed for every product on the list, and that the predictions are based on last year's deals.

Readers are told to check manufacturer stores and authorized retailers for updated offers as the event approaches. The guide frames AI as becoming part of everyday technology, citing a Pew Research Center 2026 survey that found 35% of U.S. adults own a smart speaker, 37% own a smartwatch, and 13% use a robot vacuum with AI features. It says Meta left the Ray-Ban Gen 2 and Oakley HSTN out of last year's Black Friday sale, so a cut should not be assumed. The article does not say what happens next beyond advising readers to watch for updated offers as the sales approach.

Articles.Title: 10 Best Black Friday AI Gadget Deals in 2026: Top Picks

stories.Headline: Camerimage Founder Marek Zydowicz on AI, Aronofsky and Why “Cinematographers Are Artists, Not Technicians”
stories.Summary:
Camerimage, the Polish festival devoted to cinematography, marks its 34th year this November in Torun, running from November 7 to 14. Its founder, Marek Zydowicz, who started the event in 1993 to champion cinematographers and other below-the-line artists, is speaking openly about the issues facing the industry. Those include the rise of generative AI, which has its own debates and workshops at this year's festival, along with pressure on budgets and theatrical releases. The festival has also chosen to honor Darren Aronofsky, an outspoken adopter of AI, with its director award.

Zydowicz says Camerimage will stay open to a diversity of techniques and technologies, but he draws a firm line at fully AI-generated films. Joe Walker, the editor known for Dune and 12 Years a Slave, is also being honored and will chair the Main Competition jury. Polish cinematographer Janusz Kaminski, whose Disclosure Day is screening in contention, receives THR's Visionary award. Zydowicz frames the festival's mission as defending the artistic standing of people the industry has long treated as technicians.

In the interview, Zydowicz traces the strength of Polish cinematography to history, arguing that the tradition of depicting national events during the partitions and the postwar founding of the Lodz Film School shaped it. He says artists working under communist censorship learned to convey hidden meanings through composition and the relationship between image and dialogue. He also credits the Lodz school's teaching of painting history, and generations of filmmakers who taught there, for producing a tradition now visible in Polish cinematographers' work worldwide. He explained the Aronofsky choice by pointing to more than thirty years of films that unsettle audiences and ask them to confront difficult aspects of human nature.

Zydowicz cited Requiem for a Dream, Black Swan, The Fountain and The Whale as examples of work that moves between intimacy and spectacle while encouraging viewers to notice pain that might otherwise go unseen. He said he expects the decision to spark debate, given how contentious AI remains across the industry. The article does not describe what the festival's AI workshops will cover or how the jury will assess films made with new technology. Coverage of the festival's competition and awards is likely to follow as the November 7 to 14 program unfolds.

Articles.Title: Camerimage Founder Marek Zydowicz on AI, Aronofsky and Why “Cinematographers Are Artists, Not Technicians”

stories.Headline: Amazon closed an AI educator's account after he ordered seven Nvidia DGX Spark mini-PCs, and Tim Sweeney says his GPU orders were canceled too
stories.Summary:
Amazon closed the account of Nick Saraev, an AI automation educator and YouTuber, after he tried to buy seven Nvidia DGX Spark mini-PCs. He placed four separate orders on October 31 to set up local AI models for a project, and Amazon canceled them without charging him. On November 1 he posted an Amazon email saying the account had been closed after a review, which referred to earlier verification attempts but gave no specific reason. Amazon's support account had replied to his first post offering to look into it a few hours before the closure.

Saraev wrote that buying even modest amounts of compute immediately puts a buyer on a watchlist. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney posted on November 2 that Amazon had kept accepting his ordinary orders and then canceled them shortly before delivery after he tried to buy two Nvidia graphics cards. His account was not closed. Another X user said Amazon had canceled his orders for an Asus mini-PC built on the same Grace Blackwell chip months earlier, and that he received the device only after sending documents to an account specialist.

Amazon has not publicly explained the cancellations or commented on the cases. Its conditions of use let it refuse service, terminate accounts, or cancel orders at its sole discretion. Wccftech reported that it is unconfirmed whether the cancellations reflect a glitch or an anti-scalping limit on how many units one buyer can take, and none of the reports points to a new Amazon policy. DGX Spark remained listed on Amazon, where third-party listings were priced at $8,499.99 and $9,499.99. Nvidia had already raised the price of its own Founders Edition by $700 to $4,699, which Tom's Hardware tied to a memory shortage as AI data centers absorb DRAM supply.

Articles.Title: Amazon closed an AI educator's account after he ordered seven Nvidia DGX Spark mini-PCs, and Tim Sweeney says his GPU orders were canceled too

stories.Headline: What Is Atlassian (TEAM) Telling Investors With Its AI Push And Cautious Outlook?
stories.Summary:
Atlassian, the software maker known for its collaboration tools, reported first-quarter results that management tied to strong momentum in its cloud products and newer AI features. The company also expanded its collaboration with OpenAI and introduced the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol, a framework for embedding AI agents across its collaboration tools. Revenue for the quarter reached US$1,772.15 million, and the company swung from a loss to net income of US$90.72 million. Guidance for the full year, however, reflected a more cautious revenue outlook as customers continue moving from Data Center products to cloud offerings.

Atlassian also appointed Eli Berkovitch as Chief Accounting Officer, adding a senior finance leader to its team. The article describes this as a signal of continuity on execution for the company's cloud and AI strategy. The company's market capitalization is listed at $38.9 billion, placing it among large US software peers that are also weaving AI agents into everyday workflows. The article notes that the heavy spending on AI and cloud could weigh on GAAP margins if it does not produce clear pricing power and higher recurring revenue over time.

The analysis in the article comes from Simply Wall St, which produced it with AI automation based on historical data and analyst forecasts. It states that the commentary is general in nature and does not constitute a recommendation to buy or sell any stock. The writer identifies subscription recurring revenue growth and the GAAP operating margin, which management outlined around a 5% target for the year, as the key measures to watch in the rest of fiscal 2027. Any sustained shortfall in those measures would challenge the idea that the cloud migration and AI spending are converting efficiently into earnings.

Articles.Title: What Is Atlassian (TEAM) Telling Investors With Its AI Push And Cautious Outlook?

stories.Headline: Embodied AI: Definition, Components and Research Areas
stories.Summary:
Embodied AI is a field of artificial intelligence built around an agent with a physical or simulated body that learns by perceiving and acting within an environment. A CASRAI guide, last reviewed on 8 November 2026, explains the concept by drawing on two arXiv papers. The article notes that the field lacks a single formal definition, so it attributes each framing to its source. The guide was written for researchers and research administrators.

The ICML 2024 position paper "A call for embodied AI," by Paolo, Gonzalez-Billandon and Kégl, presents embodied AI as a key step toward artificial general intelligence. It contrasts this approach with current large language models and traces the idea of embodiment through philosophy, psychology, neuroscience and robotics. Under this view, an embodied system is judged by what it does in an environment, not only by the text or images it produces. The guide reports that the paper names four essential components: perception, action, memory and learning.

The comprehensive survey by Liu and colleagues (arXiv:2407.06886, first submitted 9 July 2024 and revised 25 August 2025) treats the field as covering both physical robots and simulators. It organizes research around four targets, and the guide describes these as the areas of study the survey maps. The survey also discusses multi-modal large models, world models, datasets and open challenges. The guide adds that the two sources divide the topic differently, with one listing components inside an agent and the other listing research targets across the field.

The guide frames the position paper as arguing that embodied AI is the next step beyond large language models, while noting that the survey treats multi-modal large models as one of the technologies used in embodied systems. It advises readers to start with the position paper for the conceptual argument and the survey for the broader map. It also recommends citing the specific arXiv version read, since preprints may change after peer review. No further developments or timelines are reported in the article.

Articles.Title: Embodied AI: Definition, Components and Research Areas

stories.Headline: 300 media outlets worldwide “Cooperate to bridge AI technology gaps and ensure responsible reporting”… Joint statement announced at the 7th World Media Summit
stories.Summary:
At the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, held on the 7th of the month in the Great Hall of the People, media organizations from around the world issued a joint statement on artificial intelligence. The summit is organized by Xinhua News Agency and co-hosted with the Beijing Municipal People's Government, and this year's event ran from the 5th to the 9th under the theme of media in the digital age. About 500 participants from roughly 330 media organizations, think tanks, government departments and international bodies across 112 countries and regions attended. Park Jong-Seong, president of the Kyunghyang Shinmun, was the only Korean media executive present, and South Korea's ambassador to China, Noh Jae-Heon, also attended the opening ceremony.

The statement says AI has become a key driver of media change and that sharing technology widely is a common demand across the industry. It commits signatories to encourage the broad and responsible use of AI in media and to make sure the benefits reach outlets in countries with uneven technological capacity and different stages of development. It also calls on the press to stay objective and fair, to resist disinformation and false reporting, and to build rational channels for dialogue on global challenges. The articles do not describe any binding obligations or enforcement mechanisms attached to these commitments.

The statement was framed as a shared effort rather than the work of a single party, though the summit was hosted by Xinhua. Li Shulei, head of the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China, gave a keynote speech calling for better content quality, joint promotion of digital transformation, action on imbalances in data and algorithms, and wider cross-border media exchange. Xinhua president Fu Hua introduced an AI assistant called "Xinhua Style" and urged active adoption of AI alongside international cooperation. Reuters president Paul Bascobert said the tools have changed but the principles have not, and Park Jong-Seong said journalists will survive the AI era but that those who fail to use AI risk being pushed out.

The context is a set of concerns raised during the thematic discussions. Participants warned that gaps in infrastructure and the scarcity of large language models for non-English and minority languages could produce biased information, and speakers from the United Nations and Egypt's State Information Service stressed access to digital infrastructure and AI that reflects Global South realities. The articles note that the tension between the public's right to know and efforts to police misinformation was not explored in depth that day. The organizers had also unveiled an AI robot anchor at a pre-event on the 5th and 6th, which raised the question of job replacement that participants said makes human responsibility in journalism more important. The articles do not say what follow-up steps, if any, the signatories have planned.

Articles.Title: 300 media outlets worldwide “Cooperate to bridge AI technology gaps and ensure responsible reporting”… Joint statement announced at the 7th World Media Summit

stories.Headline: Nasdaq set to confirm correction as AI spending worries mount
stories.Summary:
The Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 4 per cent on Thursday, November 5, 2026, closing in on a confirmed correction as worries about huge AI spending and closer scrutiny of data-center expansion rattled technology stocks. The index dropped to 24,712.60, more than 10 per cent below its record closing high of 27,599.89, set on October 6. The slide wiped out the previous session's gains, which had come after Democrats won both houses of Congress. A fall of 10 per cent from the latest record close is widely treated as a correction, and this would be the Nasdaq's second of the year.

October was already painful for the index, which lost more than $2.5 trillion in market value that month. Several large tech companies are borrowing in debt markets to help pay for billions of dollars in planned spending on data centers, chips and other infrastructure for AI development. Investors have been asking how soon that spending will turn into profits, especially since tensions in the Middle East and fears of lasting inflation have kept borrowing costs high. Earnings last month from Alphabet and Meta did not calm those doubts about returns, and they added to a wider selloff in AI-linked shares.

Sameer Samana, senior global market strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute, linked part of the move to the election result. He said a switch from one party holding unified control to the other can bring uncertainty, discontinuity and abrupt policy change. He added that when Democrats looked set to win big majorities in both the House and the Senate, his firm thought markets would at least take a short pause. Investors, the report said, were weighing the chance of tougher scrutiny of further AI infrastructure buildout.

The selloff has pushed money toward other parts of the market. According to Investing.com, investors have moved toward Chinese and Indian equities and Asian sectors less reliant on technology, after semiconductor-heavy markets fell sharply following the U.S. midterms. A Hong Kong index of mainland Chinese companies rose 5.2% last week, its best showing since March 2025, while India's Nifty 50 jumped 8.6%, its largest weekly gain since 2021. Overseas investors bought a net $1.9 billion of Indian shares through Wednesday, and in South Korea attention has turned to cosmetics, entertainment, retail and food firms. Some investors still see the AI downturn as a chance to buy, but the immediate trend favors diversifying into businesses with different earnings drivers.
