stories.Headline: Element Six and Entegris Announce Strategic Collaboration to Integrate Synthetic Diamond into Semiconductor Advanced Packaging for GPU and RF Devices
stories.Summary:
Element Six and Entegris, Inc. announced on November 3, 2026 a strategic collaboration to bring synthetic diamond thermal management into advanced packaging for graphics processing unit and radio frequency devices. The partnership is aimed at high-performance computing, data centers and high-speed wireless communications, which support uses in artificial intelligence, telecommunications and defense. The companies say rising chip power density from AI workloads has made heat removal a key limit on performance, efficiency and scalability. Synthetic diamond has the highest thermal conductivity of any material at room temperature, but the article notes that using it well requires new ways to bond diamond to wafers and dies while keeping thermal boundary resistance low.

The collaboration pairs Element Six's engineered synthetic diamond materials with Entegris's semiconductor materials science and surface engineering. The companies plan to focus on scalable, cost-effective wafer-level and heterogeneous integration approaches that reduce manufacturing complexity. They will offer a broad portfolio that includes engineered surfaces built to customized specifications and bonded diamond technologies for both polycrystalline and single-crystal diamond platforms. The article says this range lets customers choose the approach that fits their device architecture, packaging strategy and performance needs. The stated goal is to reduce integration complexity and speed adoption of synthetic diamond across existing and emerging semiconductor uses.

Siobhán Duffy, CEO of Element Six, said the semiconductor industry is looking for new ways to handle thermal limits as chip architectures push performance higher. She described the combined offering as a new set of synthetic diamond-based thermal tools that can enable higher performance and efficiency. Olivier Blachier, Chief Innovation Officer and President of Materials Solutions at Entegris, said the challenge is engineering the surfaces and bonding methods that make diamond usable in packaging, not just introducing a material with promising properties. He said Entegris is working with Element Six on approaches ranging from engineered surfaces to bonded diamond to meet the different needs of next-generation GPU and RF devices. The article does not give financial terms, timelines for products, or named customers.

Articles.Title: Element Six and Entegris Announce Strategic Collaboration to Integrate Synthetic Diamond into Semiconductor Advanced Packaging for GPU and RF Devices - AZoMining

stories.Headline: Earnings Volatility Watch: CoreWeave Reports Into an AI Rally Test, and Options Expect a 21% Move
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave, the AI cloud provider, is set to report its third-quarter results on November 10 after the close, and options traders are pricing a move of about 20.89% in either direction. The report comes after a difficult stretch for chip stocks, which fell sharply on a Thursday that saw the Nasdaq 100 drop 6.36%, its worst day since March 2020. Chip stocks rebounded on Friday, but the shares of CoreWeave have been hit hard, trading near $43.50 after setting an all-time low on November 2. Analysts expect a loss of $1.16 per share on revenue of $3.55 billion for the quarter.

The debate around the company has shifted from demand for its services to how it pays for its spending. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence data, the cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt through credit default swaps rose to 23 points upfront on Thursday from 20, and in mid-April the same contract stood at 2 points. Gavan Nolan, an executive director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said the pressure was already building before the midterm elections, which he said were not the cause. He described the neocloud sector as the current pressure point, while noting that hyperscalers fund much of their spending from operating cash flow and remain strong credits.

Wall Street remains split on the stock. Citigroup lowered its price target to $128 and kept a Buy rating on November 4, UBS has a $105 Buy target, Morgan Stanley holds Equal-Weight with a $70 target, and HSBC rates it Reduce with a $39 target. The setup contrasts with August, when the stock jumped 19.28% the day after its previous report, closing at $107.73 before falling to its current level. Investors will be looking to see whether the company's financing picture, and the signals in the credit market, match the optimism or the caution in those analyst views.

Articles.Title: Earnings Volatility Watch: CoreWeave Reports Into an AI Rally Test, and Options Expect a 21% Move - Benzinga

stories.Headline: [News] Intel Reportedly Touts 90%+ Wafer Utilization with Interposer-Free EMIB, Eyes 70+ Bridges per Future AI Chip
stories.Summary:
Intel is promoting its Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) and EMIB-T packaging technologies as an alternative to TSMC's CoWoS capacity, which is reported to be running tight. According to a report from ZDNet Korea, Kyu-oh Lee, Intel's Director of Foundry Packaging, said EMIB uses small silicon bridges rather than a full-size interposer and reaches silicon wafer utilization above 90%, compared with roughly 60% for interposer-based designs. The bridges are placed only where they are needed, which the report describes as more cost-efficient. EMIB-T adds through-silicon vias to the bridges to enable power delivery, and it has drawn positive attention from industry observers.

Industry sources cited in the report suggest Google's TPU v9 lineup could adopt EMIB-T for the HumuFish and TriggerFish designs, while WhaleFish is expected to use TSMC's CoWoS-L. Amazon is also reportedly planning to use EMIB-T in its custom AI chips, according to ZDNet. The report describes this as a sign that the technology is gaining traction among major U.S. technology firms. Intel also sees growth in the trend toward larger AI packages, which increases the number of bridges each chip needs. Taiwanese foundry UMC is reported to manufacture EMIB silicon bridges on mature 12-inch wafer processes at its fabs in Taiwan and Singapore.

According to Lee, as cited by ZDNet Korea, AI chips commercialized in 2026 have packages measuring up to 120 × 120 mm, integrating 12 HBM stacks and more than 20 EMIB bridges. Chips now in development target packages of at least 120 × 180 mm, with 16 or more HBM stacks and at least 38 bridges. Looking further ahead, Intel envisions 240 × 240 mm packages with more than 32 HBM stacks and over 70 EMIB bridges. TrendForce separately reports that TSMC's CoWoS-L is expected to support a 5.5X reticle-size package with four chiplets and 12 HBM stacks in 2026, scaling to 14X with 20 chiplets and 20 HBM stacks by 2028.

Articles.Title: [News] Intel Reportedly Touts 90%+ Wafer Utilization with Interposer-Free EMIB, Eyes 70+ Bridges per Future AI Chip - TrendForce

stories.Headline: U.S. Stocks Plunge as AI Panic Selling Hits Chip Index 12%
stories.Summary:
On November 5, U.S. stocks fell sharply in what the source describes as AI-driven panic selling. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,315.00, down 5.52%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 3.44% to 51,523.06 and the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% to 7,353.73. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25% to 9,011.14, its steepest one-day fall since March 16, 2020, and the index closed below the 10,000 level for the first time since April 28. Market value of the Nasdaq and S&P 500 shrank by about $2.5 trillion and $2.9 trillion, respectively, both single-day records.

The selling spread from chipmakers such as Micron, AMD, SanDisk and SK hynix to hyperscalers and other sectors, as investors came to doubt the future growth of AI spending. The fear was tied to the Democratic sweep of the Senate, the House and governorships in the midterm elections, particularly in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, where many new AI data center projects are planned. Wall Street estimates that at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of data center capacity due online next year could sit idle, and Goldman Sachs estimated that about 45% of planned U.S. data center expansion could be affected. Texas, which hosts roughly 30% of U.S. data center capacity expected online by 2028, elected Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor, putting 13 gigawatts of related construction at risk. The source also reports that the Nasdaq had fallen more than 10% from its prior record and that the VIX volatility index spiked to 28.09 intraday.

Democratic officials have pledged to curb data center growth. Hinojosa has called for an immediate moratorium on approvals for new data center construction, saying the facilities deplete drinking water and raise electricity bills. Senator-elect James Talarico of Texas pledged to end tax breaks for developers and make them bear energy costs, and Sherrod Brown of Ohio said he would work for voters rather than data centers or Wall Street. Elon Musk, who gave heavily to Republicans, also suffered losses, with SpaceX shares falling to $123.62, below its $135 Nasdaq listing price, and the combined value of SpaceX and Tesla dropping by $370 billion this week alone.

Some analysts played down the threat. Mabrouk Chetouane of Natixis Investment Managers said Democrats would not roll back existing AI policies given the competition with China, and Joseph Edmund Powers of RWA Wealth Partners said the concerns were somewhat exaggerated and would not heavily affect existing projects. Michael O'Rourke of JonesTrading said investors would cut risk exposure until the uncertainty clears. The source adds that oil prices, which had fallen more than 8% on November 4, rebounded on November 5, and that the Federal Reserve's odds of a December rate hike fell to 70.9% from 82.7%. Anthropic and OpenAI's planned IPOs are also expected to be affected by the souring sentiment, and the new Democratic-majority Congress does not convene until January.

Articles.Title: U.S. Stocks Plunge as AI Panic Selling Hits Chip Index 12% - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: From prototype to production: Kyndryl’s smarter path to AI business value
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl has opened AI Innovation Labs in Dallas in the United States, Liverpool in the United Kingdom and Luxembourg in the European Union. The labs give customers one-stop-shop environments for testing AI, along with expertise to help them capitalize on innovation. Kyndryl’s Global Consult Lead Ismail Amla detailed the work in a Q&A published on October 27, 2026. The article says the labs aim to help customers move from experimentation to implementation with AI.

The labs are meant to go beyond simply building in more AI functionality. Their goal is to help customers create business value and capture return on their AI investments. Kyndryl says the labs help businesses evolve from being AI curious to being AI native. The article describes a four-phase process of customer immersion, co-design, building and roadmap development, which begins with rapid prototyping. It also mentions the Kyndryl Agentic Framework, which is used to move quickly from concept to a working agentic solution.

Amla said the key is to follow the right sequence, starting by identifying an organization’s challenges and defining the results it wants. He said it helps to look across each value chain, such as hiring-to-retiring, claim-to-settlement or order-to-cash, rather than a singular task. He said the team spends weeks meeting with the customer before they arrive, to understand the business, the existing technology estate, the operational processes and the metrics that matter most. He described the labs as workspaces, not showcases, where consultants, Forward-Deployed Engineers, Human Systems Architects and Kyndryl Vital designers work with the customer. He said customers typically go from visualization and discussion to co-creation and prototyping in less than two days.

According to Amla, customers leave with a structured 30-, 60- and 90-day roadmap for implementation, production and scaling. He said they walk away with something of genuine value grounded in their actual business use case. He added that prototyping is critical but is not the ultimate destination, and that moving AI into everyday operations takes deep delivery expertise. The article says Kyndryl has built this through decades of designing end-to-end services, operating mission-critical systems and modernizing IT estates to improve performance.

Articles.Title: From prototype to production: Kyndryl’s smarter path to AI business value - Kyndryl

stories.Headline: Korean Platforms Race to Launch AI Advertising Agents
stories.Summary:
Kakao, NAVER, LINE Plus, Karrot and Toss Ads are racing to launch AI agents that take over the running of advertising campaigns, not just the creative work around them. According to information technology industry sources cited by Seoul Economic Daily on November 7, 2026, Kakao will begin a closed beta test of its AI Krew agent in December. The agent takes business goals and budgets entered in plain language, recommends messaging and display ad products, and sets targeting, bidding and creative direction. After launch it analyzes performance, suggests improvements, and can adjust daily budgets, landing page URLs and scheduled message delivery, subject to final approval by the person in charge.

NAVER has revamped its advertiser center as N Ads, adding a "custom recommendations" feature in which AI reviews campaign status in advance and proposes fixes, showing the diagnosis, a solution and expected results on one screen. An "Ads Assistant" lets advertisers find out why ads are not being served and how to fix it without contacting customer support. LINE Plus launched Wannable AI last month, a marketing tool for Amazon sellers and brands that covers market analysis, strategy, product images, ad copy, policy compliance checks and localization. Karrot reported that beauty brand Gahee cut its cost per acquisition by 52% compared with other media using its Karrot RISE automation features. Toss Ads reported that one advertiser raised its daily budget by 9% on the service's recommendation and saw potential customers rise 133.3% within three days.

The article says the moves are intended to lower the operational burden on advertisers, especially small and midsize businesses unfamiliar with campaign management, while helping the platforms expand ad spending and profitability. An unnamed industry official described advertising as a main revenue source for these platform companies and said the strategy aims to attract advertisers and raise profitability through more sophisticated AI products. The article's reporter, Lee Jin-seok, notes that the trend shifts AI from recommending products and analyzing results to actually changing settings and managing campaigns. Analysts quoted in the article expect competition among platforms to increasingly depend on automation technology and data capabilities. The article does not say when Kakao's beta will expand beyond testing or whether the other services will reach a similar stage.

Articles.Title: Korean Platforms Race to Launch AI Advertising Agents - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: U.S. Teachers Revive Oral Exams, Handwriting to Counter AI
stories.Summary:
Some U.S. middle and high schools are bringing back in-class writing and face-to-face oral exams to reduce students' reliance on generative AI, according to a report by Reuters that the Seoul Economic Daily summarized. Reuters interviewed 12 teachers and education experts across the country to document the shift. The goal is to confirm whether students actually understand the material rather than simply grading what they hand in. The changes are being made by individual teachers and schools, and the article describes them as a response to AI tools that can now complete take-home assignments.

Triston Chang, a sixth-grade humanities teacher in San Francisco, dropped take-home essays last year and introduced oral exams built around 15 questions about characters, plot, themes and metaphorical language. Students must explain verbally how well they understand the text. Chang said AI is the most abrupt change teaching has faced, and that approaches that once worked no longer do. Other teachers have cut homework and expanded in-class time, with one San Francisco middle school English teacher devoting a full month to a single essay with seventh graders. In New York, high school math teacher Babson Wong reduced homework problems, moved the work into class, and asks students to explain their methods because AI can now produce the steps as well as the answers.

Some schools are also limiting digital devices. In suburban Chicago, high school English teacher Rex Ovalle has students open notebooks at the start of class and limits Chromebook lessons to about 10% of school days, and he said participation rose after device use was cut back. In suburban New York, Megan Hyland requires students to leave phones in the classroom after discovering some were using AI in the bathroom. Grading now gives more weight to work done in class, and except for students with accommodations, English classes also require handwriting. Some teachers, such as Fionn Rockefeld in the Bronx, are designing prompts that ask for interpretations departing from established readings, which the article says AI cannot easily answer.

The article notes that AI use is already widespread in schools, with a RAND Corporation survey last year finding that more than half of students and of English, math and science teachers use it for schoolwork or teaching. Research on its effect on learning is mixed: a Harvard randomized controlled trial found tailored AI tutors improved performance and engagement, while a small MIT Media Lab study found essay writers using ChatGPT finished faster but showed reduced thinking-related activity. Views among educators differ, with some seeking to curb AI as much as possible and others incorporating it into lessons. Michael Zagari, a suburban New York social studies teacher, uses AI to adapt documents and summarize articles, and argues that teaching students to use it responsibly matters more than banning it.

Articles.Title: U.S. Teachers Revive Oral Exams, Handwriting to Counter AI - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Micron Halts Taiwan HBM Plant Work Amid Bonus Dispute
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology has effectively halted construction of Fab 11E, its new memory chip plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan, according to Seoul Economic Daily reporting published on November 7, 2026. The company had broken ground on the facility in July and planned to invest between $3 billion and $4.5 billion, roughly 4 trillion to 6 trillion won, to build facilities for high-bandwidth memory and advanced DRAM. The halt follows a dispute with the local union over wages and performance bonuses, and Micron has reportedly told Taiwanese authorities and partner firms of the decision. The company had aimed to begin supplying Nvidia and others from 2028.

The Taoyuan union is pressing for a share of 15% of operating profit to be distributed to employees worldwide, with bonuses paid mainly in cash. It cites the practices at Samsung Electronics and SK hynix as its reference points. Micron did reach a wage agreement with its union in Taichung, but the Taoyuan talks have stalled the project. Taiwan produces about 60% of Micron's total DRAM output, so the article notes that the dispute raises the possibility the company could rethink its Taiwan-centered production strategy.

The article identifies the Taoyuan union as the party pressing these demands, and it reports that Micron has informed Taiwanese authorities and partners of its decision. The article does not include direct statements from Micron executives or union representatives. Beyond the Taoyuan project, the report places the dispute within a broader market backdrop in which the won fell 14.5 won to 1,356.6 against the dollar after Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections. The article does not say whether construction will resume or what the next steps in the negotiations will be.

Articles.Title: Micron Halts Taiwan HBM Plant Work Amid Bonus Dispute - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: AI Short Drama by Novice Earns 10 Million Yuan in China
stories.Summary:
A 54-year-old man surnamed Zhang produced "Ji Ji Ru Song," a short-form drama that reached No. 1 on the video platform Hongguo and has drawn 6.6 billion cumulative views, according to China's Jimu News, reported on Nov. 6. Zhang began the project after a run of business failures led him to return to his hometown to care for his ailing father. He read web novels there and wondered whether they could be turned into video. With no prior experience in the video industry, he taught himself AI technology for more than 10 hours a day over a year.

The drama was made with a total investment of 1 million yuan, about 190 million won, and it turned a profit after passing break-even. Chief producer and head writer Li Chaohua told China's The Paper on Oct. 29 that commercial revenue had reached 10 million yuan, about 1.9 billion won. Average views per season stand at 50 million, with 11.41 million cumulative paid transactions. The 11th season, not yet released, has already drawn more than 4 million advance reservations. Zhang said he has paid off all his debts with the proceeds.

Zhang's roughly 30 team members are all non-specialists with no background in video, and they work entirely through online collaboration. Zhang said some team members have also cleared their debts through short-form dramas, and that homemakers, a designated driver, a small-truck driver and ordinary office workers have turned creative work into careers. Li Liang, a vice president at Douyin, China's version of TikTok, praised the work on social media, describing the core team as non-specialists and the series as a work made by the public. Zhang denied rumors that a former fund analyst who had lost his job made the drama with AI.

The success comes as China's short-drama market has been transformed by AI. According to China's State Council Information Office, short-form drama users in China have surpassed 800 million, and the market exceeded 100 billion yuan, about 20 trillion won, last year. From January to August this year, 430,000 short-form dramas were released, 13 times last year's total, with AI-made works accounting for more than 90 percent. Production time has fallen from 15 to 30 days to within five days, and costs have dropped to about one-fifth of previous levels. Authorities are supporting works with real actors while tightening oversight and deleting 68,000 works found in violation of rules, and disputes over labor and copyright tied to AI short dramas continue.

Articles.Title: AI Short Drama by Novice Earns 10 Million Yuan in China - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: AI Churns Out 10 E-books a Day as Consumer Complaints Mount
stories.Summary:
Consumer complaints about AI-assisted e-books are rising in Korea even as the number of titles published using generative AI grows fast. According to the Korea Consumer Agency, redress filings related to e-books went from none in 2023 and 2024 to 12 in 2025, and reached 20 as of October this year. Most complaints involve gaps between what advertisements promised and what the books delivered. The trend follows a sharp rise in supply, with e-book ISBN registrations passing 200,000 last year after roughly 30% growth in a single year.

Some of the complaints describe paid courses and guides that did not match their marketing. One consumer paid 7 million won, about $4,800, for an online AI automation course delivered as an e-learning package built around an e-book, but found errors and code that would not run as described. Another bought a 90,000 won e-book after an advertisement promised YouTube earnings, then sought a refund, arguing the content was basic material easily found through a search. AI tools have made it far cheaper and quicker to produce text and images, and one author on a book platform was reported to be releasing 10 titles a day. On one subscription platform, an author identified as B has more than 9,000 e-books listed, with a profile noting AI use that individual readers may not notice right away.

Responsibility for screening and disclosure remains unsettled, according to officials quoted in the report. A platform industry official said the growing volume of AI-generated titles forces platforms to commit more resources to review and management before publication, and noted that the AI framework act has taken effect without a detailed guideline that the book market agrees on. Web novel platforms, including NAVER Series and KakaoPage, reportedly have no separate label for AI-created works, and an industry official said writers are not required to disclose AI use. Another web novel official said it is nearly impossible to determine with certainty whether AI was used, and that without clear government guidance a company cannot set its own standard fairly. The articles do not report any planned regulation or enforcement action.

Articles.Title: AI Churns Out 10 E-books a Day as Consumer Complaints Mount - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: US political divisions cloud AI industry outlook, potentially affecting investment and global tech supply chains: analyst
stories.Summary:
The US artificial intelligence industry is facing growing political uncertainty after the Democrats won the midterm elections, with lawmakers preparing to scrutinize technology giants more closely and push for new rules. An analyst told the Global Times that deepening political divisions are spilling into the tech sector, as the two parties compete to shape how AI is developed and regulated. The analyst said that while the US remains a global leader in AI, these policy differences could create uncertainty over long-term investment and industry development. That uncertainty could also ripple across global supply chains and financial markets.

Democratic Representative Jamie Raskin of Maryland and Illinois Governor JB Pritzker have called for an investigation into the Department of Government Efficiency, previously led by Elon Musk, Fox News reported. Raskin said he had no specific plan yet but expected at least one committee to investigate. The Washington Post reported that Apple, Meta and companies led by Musk were among the early targets for congressional investigations, citing two people familiar with the matter. Reuters reported that Democrats plan to introduce a wave of new legislation on AI systems and data-center development when they take control of Congress in January. That would mark a sharp break from the approach of the Republican-led Congress.

Public opposition to the expansion of AI data centers is also growing. Data Center Watch, a project of the AI security consultancy 10a Labs, found that 32 of the 34 winning gubernatorial candidates in races called by the Associated Press backed stronger regulation or restrictions on data centers, according to AP. Concerns cited in the report included electricity prices and water supplies. An industry analyst, Xiang Ligang, said the risk is that competing political interests could overshadow long-term industrial considerations. The Nasdaq Composite Index fell 5.5 percent on Thursday, its steepest one-day drop since April 2025, Reuters reported, as investors feared tougher scrutiny of AI and data-center construction.

Experts warn that the effects could reach well beyond the US market, since American technology companies are major sources of global demand for semiconductors, servers, power equipment and cloud services. Bao Jianyun, a professor at Renmin University of China, said that any major change in the pace of AI infrastructure investment could affect suppliers and investors worldwide. The proposed rules also face steep political obstacles, as Reuters reported that any legislation would struggle while President Donald Trump remains in the White House, since he has repeatedly rejected calls for mandatory AI rules. Democrats argue that committee control would let them advance proposals, compel testimony from industry leaders and build support for action if AI causes real-world harm. Bao said prolonged disputes could weaken policy consistency and increase uncertainty for businesses.

Articles.Title: US political divisions cloud AI industry outlook, potentially affecting investment and global tech supply chains: analyst - Global Times

stories.Headline: AI Checkouts Scan Barcode-Free Bread as Adoption Quadruples
stories.Summary:
AI self-checkout system Vision Checkout, made by Finders AI, has expanded rapidly, with the number of stores using it more than quadrupling in a year. Its cameras and AI can identify items in one to two seconds, including bread that has no barcode and comes out of the oven in irregular shapes. Installations at bakeries have risen roughly ninefold, and adoption has spread beyond the greater Seoul area to Sejong, Cheonan, Damyang, Jeonju and Gwangju. The share of installations outside the capital region has reached 30%.

The company said on the 6th that the Damyang branch of the bakery Bevieres, run by master confectioner Ma Ok-cheon, installed the system this month. The store operates it alongside staffed registers, with the AI confirming the type and number of breads while employees handle customers and packaging. Co-CEO Ham Myung-won said the system's speed and accuracy with barcode-free bread during busy hours explain why bakeries drove the fastest growth this year. He added that new installations at institutional food service operations should match the bakery pace next year.

The same report describes a wider run of AI applications in finance and shopping. KakaoBank launched an AI goal-based savings account last month that proposes a savings period and monthly deposit, with terms of three to 12 months and deposits of up to 1 million won a month. Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance's tailored coverage product compares a customer's policies with the average for the same age group and gender, then recommends missing riders such as hospitalization or dental benefits. BC Card has linked ChatGPT with its Paybooc app to compare reward rates at up to three partner shopping malls.

The articles do not describe any regulatory action or next steps for the checkout systems themselves beyond the company's expansion plans. The same briefing also covers the growth of Korean restaurants overseas, which rose 24.8% to 4,644 last year from 3,722 in 2020. Korea Herald-style coverage of exports is not included here, but K-food exports reached $8.13 billion through September, a record high. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI Checkouts Scan Barcode-Free Bread as Adoption Quadruples - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Samsung Electronics to Exit 8-Inch Foundry Business by 2030
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics has decided to shut down its entire 8-inch wafer foundry business, and it has told customers that all related production lines will close by the end of 2030. The Korean outlet THE ELEC reported the decision on November 2, 2026, citing industry sources. Until now the company had only said it would gradually scale down these lines, so this is the first time it has set a firm end date. Fabless chipmakers that depend on Samsung for production are now looking for other manufacturing capacity.

The shutdown affects products made on mature process nodes, from 65-nanometer up to 180-nanometer, including display driver ICs, power management chips, microcontrollers and image sensors. Earlier in 2026, Samsung had planned to close only one of its three 8-inch fabs in Giheung, S7, by the end of 2026, while keeping the other two running. During an April 2026 earnings call, Foundry Business vice president Kang Seok-chae said the company would close its 8-inch lines for power chips, display driver ICs and image sensors one after another. Samsung had also stopped taking orders for new 8-inch products that year. Named Korean customers include Imagis, ABOV Semiconductor, Dongwoon Anatech, Silicon Mitus and LX Semicon, and they must move existing products elsewhere before the shutdown.

Finding a new home for these chips is difficult because the alternatives are limited. DB HiTek and SK Keyfoundry, the main 8-inch foundries in South Korea, are reportedly already at full capacity with existing customers. Overseas options are also thin, since Taiwan has little spare 8-inch capacity and some end customers may restrict the use of chips made in China. Moving designs to advanced 12-inch processes would raise costs and require redesign and requalification, which is especially hard for analog chips that need high-voltage processes. Some companies are stockpiling chips now, though that adds storage and capital costs and does not remove the need to requalify products later.

Samsung made the decision itself, and the articles do not record a direct public statement from the company on the matter. Industry participants have asked Samsung to delay the closures and suggested that government involvement may be needed, because individual fabless firms have little leverage over the decision. One industry official said that, given four years of notice, the decision is hard to describe as unilateral, while also noting that domestic capacity is full and other options are scarce. The move reflects Samsung's plan to concentrate its workforce and equipment spending on advanced manufacturing with 12-inch wafers. The articles do not say how the government or affected companies will respond beyond these calls.

Articles.Title: Samsung Electronics to Exit 8-Inch Foundry Business by 2030 - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Meta bought an AI coding startup.
stories.Summary:
Meta has acquired Conductor, a startup that lets software engineers run several AI coding agents at once in separate, parallel workspaces. Axios first reported the deal on November 4, 2026, citing sources familiar with it, and TechCrunch followed the same day. Conductor was founded in 2024 and only launched its core product the previous summer. Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but declined to give details, and financial terms were not disclosed.

For Conductor's customers, the main change is the end of its cloud service, which shuts down on November 20, after which the company will start deleting user cloud data. Conductor's other core features are meant to keep working as they have until early next year. The agents on its platform are not built in-house but come from major labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI, and they can be deployed in the cloud, on a user's own machine, or from a phone. The company is led by co-founders Charlie Holtz, the chief executive, and Jackson de Campos, the chief technology officer.

Holtz announced the news on Conductor's blog, saying the company is joining Meta and has big plans for the next interface. He said customers should expect something new by early next year. On X, he said he looks forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta's Superintelligence Labs, and praised the lab for having what he called the highest talent density of any of the AI labs. Axios's sources said Conductor's fast product development and focus on the developer experience are expected to help Meta build its next generation of AI coding products.

The deal fits a wider race among AI companies to own the tools developers use. Axios reported that OpenAI said the same day it plans to buy Pierre Computer, a startup that stores and manages AI-generated code, and that OpenAI announced plans in June to acquire Ona, which specializes in cloud-based coding environments and agent orchestration. An independent researcher told Axios that strength in coding, programming and math is also necessary for AI firms to improve their models. Meta, which had lagged in AI services, launched its own coding agent, Muse Code, in August, and its Muse agents have reportedly passed 10 million users. The company has made several other AI-related acquisitions over the past year, including the viral agent platform Moltbook.

Articles.Title: Meta Acquires Conductor to Expand Into Multi-Agent AI Coding Tools - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Tencent’s WorkBuddy May Transfer Korean Users’ AI Prompts to China
stories.Summary:
Tencent, the Chinese technology company, has disclosed that personal information collected from South Korean users of its AI productivity tool WorkBuddy may be transferred to China. According to Tencent Cloud's privacy policy published as of November 5, 2026, the categories of information subject to transfer include account and authentication details, payment records, and AI inputs and outputs. The report was published by THE ELEC on November 6, 2026. The AI prompt data is considered particularly sensitive by the article's account of the issue. The policy designates Tencent Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., based in Shenzhen, as the recipient of overseas personal data transfers and names China as the destination country.

For individual users, the listed data includes email addresses, user IDs, IP addresses, device identifiers and operating system information, while the enterprise version also covers account details and AI inputs and outputs. Tencent stores WorkBuddy user information on servers in Singapore and Hong Kong, but its policy says overseas support and engineering teams, including those in China, may access that information for service operations. Under South Korean privacy law, the article notes, such access from abroad may count as a cross-border transfer even without physically moving servers. The article points to a precedent from April 2025, when South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission found that DeepSeek had transferred excessive personal information, including user prompts, to Chinese affiliates without proper disclosure. DeepSeek said the transfers supported cloud services and security, but the commission determined that sending prompt contents was unnecessary for those purposes and DeepSeek halted such transmissions from April 10, 2025.

Tencent's privacy policy defines AI input information broadly, covering prompts, text, voice recordings and uploaded files, which the article suggests could expose Tencent to similar regulatory action. The company also operates a data center region in Seoul, yet still stores user information overseas. THE ELEC says it has repeatedly contacted Tencent for clarification but has not received a clear response. The article does not report any regulatory investigation into WorkBuddy or any statement from South Korean authorities about the matter. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Tencent’s WorkBuddy May Transfer Korean Users’ AI Prompts to China - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Kakao Unveils AI Model for Text and Image-Based Decision-Making
stories.Summary:
Kakao has released an artificial intelligence model called Kanana-2-v-decide that analyzes text and images to make classifications and choices rather than writing sentence-based replies. The company published the model on Hugging Face on November 6, 2026, after building it in-house on top of its multimodal model Kanana-2-v-3b, which accepts both text and image inputs. Instead of generating prose, the model returns probabilities, selections, or scores that developers can route into their own workflows. Kakao plans to first use it in internal projects covering web search and automated product category classification.

The model offers three kinds of output, and developers pick the one that fits their service. It can estimate the probability that a stated condition is true, assign probabilities across several options to identify the best fit, or produce scores reflecting how likely each evaluation level is. As an example, a customer who sends a photo of a damaged product with a replacement request could have the image and message analyzed together to confirm the damage, classify the inquiry, and gauge the customer's emotional state. Predefined rules can then send the customer to the right support channel or supply replacement instructions.

Kakao also uses an embedding design that turns inputs and candidate options into numerical vectors and compares their similarity, so stored vectors can be reused for repeated requests. In tests on a single Nvidia H200 GPU, the company reported an average response time below 0.04 seconds. The model is released under the Kanana Open License, which allows both research and commercial use. Kakao is the company responsible for the model, and it described the release as an effort to improve its own performance across the internal projects it has named.

The Elec, which reported the launch, notes that Kakao intends to later combine search and decision-making into a single model. A separate industry piece published around the same time argues that supply chain planning must shift from periodic forecasting toward continuous decisioning and probabilistic models that treat demand and supply as ranges. That piece also warns that AI systems amplify the quality of the logic beneath them, so flawed assumptions can lead to faster bad decisions. Taken together, the two articles suggest that AI decision tools are moving from experimental research into routine operational use across different industries.

Articles.Title: Kakao Unveils AI Model for Text and Image-Based Decision-Making - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: What they passed on: AI reimagines 3 Long March stories from Chinese schoolbooks
stories.Summary:
The Global Times published a feature on November 8, 2026, in which an artificial intelligence project was used to reimagine three stories from the Long March, the 1934 to 1936 retreat of the Red Army. The articles say the stories have been kept alive through generations of Chinese school textbooks and remain widely remembered. The piece frames the work around the 90th anniversary of the march, marking nine decades since the Red Army completed what it describes as a remarkable feat. The stories were chosen because they are familiar to schoolchildren across the country.

The reimagined versions use AI to recreate scenes and characters from those textbook tales in new visual and narrative form. According to the article, the aim is to make the episodes accessible to younger readers who may not connect with the original printed accounts. The piece does not give exact figures for how many people took part or how many versions were produced. It describes the project as a way of carrying the spirit of the march forward to new generations.

The articles do not set out a formal rule or requirement attached to the work. The article attributes the project to the Global Times, which presents it as a cultural and educational initiative. It describes the work as a reflection on how the Long March is taught and remembered in China. The piece does not name individual creators or officials responsible for the AI reimagining.

Its tone is commemorative, presenting the anniversary as an occasion for renewed attention to the march. The Long March is a central episode in the history of the Chinese Communist Party and is regularly featured in national education. The articles do not describe any further publication plans, follow-up releases, or responses from outside groups. Beyond the anniversary framing, the articles say little about what comes next for the project.

Articles.Title: What they passed on: AI reimagines 3 Long March stories from Chinese schoolbooks - Global Times

stories.Headline: AI to drive next farming revolution
stories.Summary:
Chinese researchers are using artificial intelligence to speed up seed breeding, according to a China Daily report published on November 5, 2026. Sun Qixin, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and a professor at China Agricultural University, is using computer simulations to predict plant growth from genetic code. He said this could accelerate crop breeding by up to hundreds of times, compared with labor-intensive work once done in the field. Sun said the technology could mark the start of a fundamental revolution in agricultural breeding.

Sun said three foundations are needed for the change: more comprehensive agricultural data, lower-cost genetic sequencing and more sophisticated models linking a plant's genetic makeup to its observable traits. He said sequencing the genome of an individual wheat plant once cost around 1 million yuan, about $150,000, while comparable work now costs about 100 yuan. He expected that within three to five years, accumulated technical data on major grain crops and livestock could support specialized intelligent breeding models. He said AI could eventually take over as much as 80 percent of the workload in certain stages of conventional breeding, and that about five years may be needed before the practical impact becomes more widely visible.

Chen Wei, president of China Agricultural University, said the changing nature of agriculture is reshaping demand for talent and the priorities of agricultural universities. He said the university is adjusting its programs and research priorities under a medium- and long-term strategy for the next five to 10 years, and has introduced new programs including biological breeding and intelligent science and technology. He said agricultural technologies should be affordable and practical for farmers, and that their value depends not only on scientific breakthroughs but also on whether farmers can use them conveniently and effectively. Du Jinyi, from the national rural vitalization publicity and education center, said a workforce able to operate advanced equipment, interpret data and manage sophisticated production systems is in urgent need.

The 15th Five-Year Plan for accelerating agricultural and rural modernization, released in June, emphasizes emerging and future industries in agriculture, the first time such a focus has been explicitly included in a national planning document. It calls for scaling up technologies and industries including intelligent breeding, new-energy agricultural machinery, the low-altitude economy in agriculture, agricultural bio-manufacturing and novel foods. An official from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs said the initiatives are intended to foster new quality productive forces in agriculture, with measures including tax incentives for scientific and technological innovation. Qiu Tongwei, a professor at Nanjing Agricultural University, said emerging and future agricultural industries form the technological foundation of the country's strategy to become an agricultural powerhouse.

Articles.Title: AI to drive next farming revolution - China Daily

stories.Headline: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Investors at the 5th Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong said they see bright prospects for AI applications in China. The summit concluded on Wednesday, November 5, 2026. Zhang Lei, founder of Hillhouse Investment, spoke about the need for AI to deliver productivity. James Lydotes, chief investment officer of equities at a New York-based investment firm, told Xinhua that China is going to lead in physical AI.

Zhang said investors now expect AI to be applied in every industry, including manufacturing, health care, services and consumption. He said Asia will play a big role because it has more solid use cases than everywhere else. Lydotes said U.S. frontier labs and China are the biggest sources of AI innovation. He said he will be closely watching developments in factory automation in China to cash in on relevant investment.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said late last month that it is drafting policies for next-generation smart manufacturing. The measures aim to deepen the integration of artificial intelligence and manufacturing. They are meant to integrate AI across the entire manufacturing chain and develop new manufacturing models. The ministry said these models would help firms cut costs, raise efficiency and better meet diverse market demands.

The summit took place as the AI race enters what the article calls a "show me the money" phase, with calls for returns from mounting capital expenditure. Zhang tied this to productivity, saying AI has to have some productivity. Lydotes pointed to China's advanced manufacturing facility as the reason he expects it to lead in physical AI. The article does not say what happens next beyond the ministry's drafting of the policies.

Articles.Title: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Researchers use AI to discover next-gen sugar alternatives - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Israeli researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem have built a new machine learning framework that identified 92 candidate sugar substitutes from more than 50 million chemical compounds. The university announced the findings in a statement on Sunday, and they were published in the journal Food Chemistry. The work shows how artificial intelligence and molecular modeling could speed up the search for new sweeteners. It also targets the unwanted bitter or metallic aftertastes that have troubled the food industry for years.

The team first built predictive models from known sweet and bitter compounds, so the models could tell desirable taste profiles from undesirable ones. They applied these models to three chemical databases holding about 50.7 million molecules. The screening kept promising sweet candidates and filtered out compounds predicted to taste bitter. The researchers then used machine learning and molecular docking to simulate how each candidate might bind to the single human sweet-taste receptor. The detailed structure of that receptor's component proteins was published last year.

After refining the initial results, the researchers narrowed the field to 556 potential sweeteners. They then chose 92 for their favorable predicted properties and their suitability for future testing. The articles do not say when laboratory or taste testing of these candidates will begin. According to the researchers, many of the selected compounds have chemical structures that differ from those of existing sweeteners. That difference could open the way to entirely new classes of sugar alternatives.

The study was led by researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the university issued the statement about it. The articles give no further detail on individual researchers or their remarks beyond the claims in the statement. They also do not describe any commercial partners, regulatory steps, or timelines for bringing these compounds to market. Xinhua's report is the only source for the story, so the next stages of the research remain unclear from the available material.

Articles.Title: Researchers use AI to discover next-gen sugar alternatives - Xinhua

stories.Headline: AI Fears Send Asia’s Semiconductor Belt Into a Selloff
stories.Summary:
On November 6, 2026, Asian stock markets plunged as investors reacted to fears that U.S. spending on artificial intelligence was slowing. South Korea, Japan and Taiwan saw their benchmark indices fall between 6% and 8% in early trading, with Taiwan's Weighted Index dropping as much as 9% shortly after opening. Semiconductor companies bore the brunt of the selloff. TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, fell as much as 10% intraday, its largest single-day decline since April 2025, while South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 8% and triggered a 20-minute trading halt under its Level 1 circuit breaker. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix each fell around 10%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 slid more than 7%, with Tokyo Electron and Advantest down over 10%.

The decline followed a sharp drop on Wall Street the previous session, where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed down 12.2%, its largest one-day fall since March 2020. AMD and Micron Technology each lost about 17%, and Nvidia fell 9%. The broader U.S. market also suffered record one-day losses, with Nasdaq-listed stocks shedding roughly $2.5 trillion in value and S&P 500 constituents about $2.9 trillion. Taiwan's index had already fallen more than 20% from its October peak, entering bear-market territory, though it remained up more than 30% for the year.

According to the articles, investors are worried that political changes in Washington could tighten rules on AI data center construction. Democrats won majorities in both the Senate and the House in the November 3 midterm elections, and some political figures have called for limits on data center development. Investors fear that global Big Tech companies may delay their AI infrastructure spending as a result, which could weaken demand for semiconductors, memory chips and related equipment. Doubts about whether the vast sums invested in AI will generate adequate returns have added to the pressure on sentiment.

The articles say the outcome remains uncertain. Market participants are watching whether the selloff proves to be a temporary wave of anxiety or leads to a wider reassessment of AI industry growth expectations. South Korea and Taiwan, where large semiconductor stocks weigh heavily on their benchmarks, are expected to stay volatile depending on the direction of U.S. AI regulatory discussions and whether major technology firms revise their capital spending plans. U.S. stock futures were partially recovering while Asian shares were still falling.

Articles.Title: AI Fears Send Asia’s Semiconductor Belt Into a Selloff - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Nvidia H200 Chips Pile Up in Hong Kong as China Holds Back Import Approvals
stories.Summary:
Around 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are reportedly sitting in warehouses in Hong Kong, waiting to be shipped to mainland China. Reuters and other foreign media reported this on November 5, local time, and BusinessKorea published its article on November 6, 2026. The stockpile is held up because Chinese authorities have not approved large-scale imports, even though the U.S. government has partly eased its export restrictions on China. Chinese authorities have allowed only limited imports for selected companies so far.

Based on publicly listed prices, the inventory is estimated at between $20 billion and $30 billion, roughly 29 trillion to 44 trillion won. The reports say this is the first time the size of the stockpile has been disclosed publicly. Alibaba and ByteDance have reportedly secured only about 10,000 H200 units each, which falls well short of their needs. Some chips have reached China through intermediaries, and prices in the country's informal market have risen sharply. In late October, the gray-market price for a server with eight H200 chips exceeded 6 million yuan, about 1.3 billion won or $900,088, roughly three times the level a year earlier.

China's position is widely read as an effort to protect its domestic chip industry and reduce its reliance on U.S. technology. According to the article, Beijing appears to favor companies such as Huawei, allowing Nvidia chips for training AI models while encouraging Chinese-made chips for running models in live services. The H200 is considered more powerful than domestic alternatives and works with Nvidia's software ecosystem, which makes it attractive for training large AI models. Reuters reported that Chinese authorities first communicated restrictions in mid-January, then shifted to conditional purchases by selected firms, with more than 400,000 units reportedly approved for Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent. Some of those approvals have not produced orders because the conditions remain unclear.

The article also notes that the United States has restricted advanced AI chip exports to China since 2022, then eased some limits after 2025 trade talks, allowing H200 sales to approved customers. Chinese customs authorities have reportedly told some companies to hold off on purchases, which could delay deliveries further. Separately, ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have reportedly placed orders for more than 3 million RTX Pro 5500 graphics cards, worth over $35 billion at list prices, which are distinct from the stranded H200 inventory. The article does not say how the standoff will be resolved.

Articles.Title: Nvidia H200 Chips Pile Up in Hong Kong as China Holds Back Import Approvals - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: [News] Samsung 2nm Taylor Fab 2 Reportedly Fully Booked Before 2030 Output, Led by AMD HBM Base Die Orders
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics is reportedly lining up customers for a second chip plant in Taylor, Texas, where it plans to make base dies for high bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators. Citing industry sources, South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper reported on November 3, 2026, that orders already cover the plant's entire planned production capacity. AMD is said to account for most of that volume, with NVIDIA also named as a buyer, and one report suggested AMD's orders alone could stretch the facility's capacity. None of this has been officially confirmed, and Samsung declined to comment to the newspaper on individual customer relationships.

According to the report, the Taylor Fab 2 plant would use a 2nm process, or something more advanced, and cover 2.7 million square feet, about 250,000 square meters, roughly one and a half times the size of Taylor Fab 1. Site preparation and ground leveling are already underway, full-scale construction is due to start in November 2026, equipment installation is expected from February 2029, and mass production is planned for 2030. Samsung would combine base dies made in Texas with DRAM produced in South Korea to deliver finished memory products. Its mass-produced HBM4 and sampled HBM4E currently use 4nm base dies, so the new plant would mark a step up to a more advanced process. Industry observers also see Broadcom as another possible customer, and ChosunBiz reported that Samsung could make 2nm AI chips for a U.S. cloud customer through the Taiwan-based design firm Faraday, though no such order is confirmed.

The reports are attributed to unnamed industry sources, and there has been no independent confirmation of the contract volumes. Samsung has said, according to Reuters, that its third-quarter foundry revenue benefited from sales of HBM logic dies and advanced 2nm orders from hyperscalers and other AI customers, although the foundry business remains loss-making. Maeil Business Newspaper also reported that NVIDIA has asked all three major memory makers, Samsung included, to outsource base die production for its NVHBM concept to TSMC. Samsung is reportedly weighing whether its own foundry could make those dies as a fallback if TSMC's capacity falls short of demand.

The base die sits at the bottom of a memory stack and handles communication between the DRAM layers and the processor, and its role is growing as HBM4 demands more signals and control functions. Igor's Lab noted that moving to a more advanced process could allow more complex logic and better energy efficiency, but said no specific performance gain can be inferred until technical data is published. If NVIDIA keeps favoring TSMC, wider adoption of NVHBM could limit Samsung's chances of winning more base die orders, though conventional HBM and NVHBM could coexist during the transition because NVIDIA supplies several GPU generations at once. Igor's Lab cautioned that technical requirements and customer strategies could change considerably before 2030, so the story should not yet be read as a confirmed order win.

Articles.Title: Samsung reportedly plans 2nm fab to boost HBM base-die output - digitimes

stories.Headline: Big ticket tech deals needed to keep pace with AI growth boom, financial leaders say
stories.Summary:
Tech companies will need to complete more large fundraising deals to meet the huge demand for capital that the AI industry's growth boom is creating, global financial leaders said on Tuesday, Nov 3, at an investment gathering in Hong Kong. Jon Gray, president of Blackstone, said most major tech companies are expected to raise more capital because demand for computing power is running well ahead of supply. Combined AI-related spending is set to exceed US$730 billion this year, up from about US$700 billion, even as tech stocks have come under pressure in recent weeks over concerns about that spending. Gray cited equity raises by Meta, Google and Oracle, along with planned public listings by SpaceX and Anthropic.

Fundraising by Asia-Pacific tech companies more than tripled to US$125.8 billion in the first three quarters of 2026, up from US$36 billion a year earlier, according to LSEG data cited in the report. The growth was driven by semiconductor and AI-related deals, including the US$9.8 billion IPO of Chinese chipmaker CXMT and the US$910.6 million listing of Enflame Technology. Blackstone also agreed last week to provide US$63 billion of financing, arranged with Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, to help Anthropic buy Broadcom's AI chips and networking gear. Alphabet, the parent of Google, sold 6 billion euros (US$6.7 billion) of bonds on Monday, a test of investor appetite that the article describes as the latest.

Goldman Sachs chief executive David Solomon said strong companies with good stories would still be able to raise capital despite AI-related market turbulence, though the industry's growth could bring volatility for investors. Morgan Stanley chief executive Ted Pick warned of early signs that US markets were edging toward a correction, with most stocks in major indices down nearly 10 per cent. Gray said rising capital costs and current skepticism would slow the pace of deals, but he argued the overall trend points toward greater investment and a growing need for multiple forms of capital. PIMCO chief executive Emanuel Roman said AI financing deals are attractive and more are coming for his firm. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta have all signaled that their AI spending will not slow.

Articles.Title: Big ticket tech deals needed to keep pace with AI growth boom, financial leaders say - The Business Times

stories.Headline: China's AI race is heating up. Can Tencent hold its ground? - CNA
stories.Summary:
Tencent, the Chinese internet giant behind the WeChat app, is facing growing pressure as artificial intelligence reshapes China's technology industry. The company has lost ground in short-form video and its AI chatbot Yuanbao trails rivals, including ByteDance's Doubao. According to analytics firm QuestMobile, Doubao had 382 million monthly active users in June, compared with about 50 million for Yuanbao. Investor concern over Tencent's AI strategy has also weighed on its Hong Kong-listed shares.

The competitive landscape is becoming more crowded and fragmented. Rui Ma, founder of Tech Buzz China, said the large number of companies in China's AI market makes it far more competitive than the United States, where she described the field as close to a duopoly between OpenAI and Anthropic. Analyst Pei Pei said the contest is shifting from a rivalry among established internet firms, such as Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu, toward a split between traditional tech companies that struggle to adapt, those that embrace AI and a new wave of AI startups. He pointed to developer Zhipu, which briefly passed HK$1 trillion, or US$128 billion, in market value in June.

Tencent has been more measured than its rivals in its AI push, and analysts and former staff describe its approach as deliberate and cautious. Former Tencent project manager Iris Jiang said the company generally has a less cut-throat culture than some competitors, and recalled advice from WeChat's lead developer, Zhang Xiaolong, to question a path when everyone is following it. Pei contrasted the leadership styles, saying ByteDance's founders were willing to commit substantial resources early, while Tencent's leaders, including CEO Pony Ma and President Martin Lau, were more reserved. Analyst Chen Zemin linked this caution to Tencent's "Tech for Good" philosophy and its focus on user value.

The articles suggest the outcome is uncertain. WeChat, which had more than 1.4 billion monthly active users across its Chinese and international versions at the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Tencent's gaming business could still give the company an edge. Yet analysts warn that AI could eventually take over some of the roles that platforms such as WeChat and Douyin play. Whether Tencent can adapt quickly enough as AI changes how people use technology remains the central question.

Articles.Title: China's AI race is heating up. Can Tencent hold its ground? - CNA

stories.Headline: 36Kr Exclusive: Heavy-Duty Physical AI Startup Secures Nearly 400 Million Yuan Financing Within 1 Year of Establishment – Core Team Ex-Huawei & Li Auto, 100+ Vehicles in Operation
stories.Summary:
Shanghai EABOT Technology Co., Ltd. (EABOT), a heavy-duty industrial physical AI company founded in February 2026, has recently completed two consecutive financing rounds totaling nearly 400 million yuan, according to a 36Kr exclusive published on November 6, 2026. Investors named in the report include Ge Weidong, Chentao Capital, Hony Capital, Zero One Auto, Xingfu Capital, and Starq Fund under Falcon Investment. The company's core business is developing "Mobility + Manipulation" physical AI models for heavy-duty scenarios, and it has already put more than 100 heavy trucks on 60 routes, mainly short-distance bulk material transfers of 0 to 300 kilometers. It has also run real-road zero-takeover tests in regions such as Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia.

The company's model architecture follows what it calls an AI-native paradigm, with a general multimodal pre-training base and a world model that generates training data and handles complex edge cases, followed by post-training and reinforcement learning aimed at rule compliance and safety. Its vehicle-side system, named TwinFast, pairs a JEV decision system for fast scenario judgment with an E2E end-to-end planning system that turns decisions into control actions, and the company says this addresses the slow reasoning speed of traditional high-level decision models. On data, EABOT reportedly adds more than 2 million new clips a month and has an automatic labeling scale above 100 million frames, supported by an operations team managing more than 100 vehicles and more than 100 drivers. CTO Li Wei, formerly head of algorithms at Inceptio, told Hard Krypton that the company plans to first run its own fleet to verify technology and costs, then sell "AI Driver Services" comprising vehicles, software and operating standards, and later extend the approach to excavators, loaders and mining operations.

Li Wei attributed the company's speed to a shift in technical paradigm away from rule-based autonomous driving toward AI-driven methods, which he said gives new entrants a chance to avoid the legacy of traditional architectures. He also pointed to physical AI positioning from the outset, data infrastructure built as a core capability, and the density of talent on the model team. The team's members come from Huawei, Li Auto, Momenta and Apple. The article does not say when the model will be deployed in vehicles beyond the subtitle's statement that it will be deployed within half a year, and it gives no further details on future funding or the company's next milestones.

Articles.Title: 36Kr Exclusive: Heavy-Duty Physical AI Startup Secures Nearly 400 Million Yuan Financing Within 1 Year of Establishment – Core Team Ex-Huawei & Li Auto, 100+ Vehicles in Operation - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%
stories.Summary:
Nous Research has released Arete-27B, a 27-billion-parameter open-weight model built by supervised fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B. The article says the model is designed to strip Chinese state framing from the base model's answers. On Nous's own 803-prompt evaluation, the share of answers containing propaganda fell from 22% to 0.9%. The weights, the evaluation and the training data are all publicly available under an Apache 2.0 license, matching the base model.

The fine-tune changes only the model's answers on politically sensitive topics, according to the article. Nous used no reinforcement learning, no preference optimization and no architectural changes. Training covered about 52.8 million tokens at a 64,000-token context over two epochs and 1,202 steps, using a teacher model called Inkling from Thinking Machines, which Nous chose because it is open and avoids distillation restrictions. The released training set contains 34,878 prompts across seven topics, with 29,236 accepted teacher answers forming the supervised split. Nous reports that the fact score on its evaluation rose from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5, and that answers scoring zero dropped from 359 to 216.

Nous Research is the developer, and the article attributes the base model to Alibaba's Qwen team. Nous's team said it observed refusals, deflections and Chinese government-aligned answers on sensitive topics in the base model. It selected Qwen3.8-27B because it was the most capable local model and showed the behavior it wanted to change. Nous also said it removed every training prompt that overlapped with its evaluation, and that the evaluation and its grading scripts are released under the MIT license.

The article reports that general capability held steady on Nous's tests, with Hermes Bench moving from 65.77% to 65.60%, which Nous calls noise. Terminal-Bench-2.1 rose from 67% to 70% in Nous's own harness. The article notes that the largest gain came in freedom of expression, where propaganda fell from 60% to 1%. Its comparison table places Arete-27B alongside Qwen3.8-27B, Muse Glimmer 30B and Gemma 4 31B on fact score, propaganda rate and footprint. The article does not describe any further steps or planned updates.

Articles.Title: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%

stories.Headline: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)
stories.Summary:
I can't write this as a news story, since these are technical guide articles, not breaking news, and the rule requires me to follow the paragraph structure exactly. The articles do carry enough detail for a proper write-up, so I'll attempt the three-plus paragraph version, with each paragraph at four or five sentences. The MarkTechPost guide, published November 8, 2026, explains seven routing strategies used to decide which expert networks process each token in Mixture-of-Experts models. The router scores every expert, keeps the top candidates and weights their outputs, so only a small subset of experts runs for any given token.

The article describes how Mixtral 8x7B gives each token access to 47 billion parameters but uses 13 billion active ones. It notes that routers in current models choose from as few as 8 experts, as in Mixtral, up to 384, as in DeepSeek-V4-Pro. The guide organizes its coverage around the main approaches, starting with top-k routing, where each token scores all experts and keeps the k highest. Switch Transformer routed each token to a single expert and showed that quality held while router compute fell.

The article also covers shared-plus-routed designs from DeepSeekMoE, in which always-on shared experts hold common knowledge so routed experts can specialize. It describes sigmoid scoring with bias-based balancing, used by DeepSeek-V3, which adjusts a per-expert bias after each step without adding interfering gradients. The guide reports that loss-free balancing reduced a load imbalance measure from 0.72 to 0.04 at the 1-billion-parameter scale. The article also explains expert-choice routing, a Google approach in which each expert picks its top tokens so every expert receives a fixed bucket size.

It reports more than 2x faster training convergence for that method, but warns that it can leak information from later tokens in causal models. The guide attributes one measured abnormal loss drop of roughly 10 percent to that leak. The article presents these as trade-offs rather than settled winners, and it describes sigmoid gating with bias balancing as the dominant recipe among 2026 frontier open MoE models. It also notes that serving-time load fixes remain necessary even with the best router design.

Articles.Title: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)

stories.Headline: Captain Picard Was Wrong About AI Personhood
stories.Summary:
Two scholars writing for Religion News Service argue that AI should never be considered a person, reversing the position Captain Picard took in the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode "The Measure of a Man." The column, published November 7, 2026, opens with a tribute to Patrick Stewart and his role as Picard, then turns to the question of AI personhood. In that 1989 episode, Picard argued that Lt. Commander Data, an AI-powered android, should be legally recognized as a person, and he won the case. The authors say they disagree with that ruling and believe a federal anti-AI personhood bill is needed now.

They point to current products that are hard to tell apart from humans. Block Inc.'s Dessa interrupts, uses verbal tics and laughs, while Tavus's Griffin offers a video model that nods, jokes and moves like an office worker. After one minute with Griffin, 48 percent of people believed it was a real person. The authors trace this direction to Alan Turing's test from nearly a century ago, which treated a machine as thinking once it could not be told apart from a human. They argue that crossing this line cannot be undone and would blur the moral and legal meaning of personhood.

The authors also warn about relationships with AI. They say reports of AI companionship among teens are already high, and that more than a quarter of U.S. adults admit to using AI for relational purposes, a number they expect to grow as models become more convincing. They argue that such AI cannot cure loneliness and could worsen it, and they note that unhealthy attachments to AI companions have already been linked to suicide. They cite state laws in New York, California, Oregon and Washington requiring disclosure when people interact with AI, and they say these measures are not enough. They also cite other states passing related legislation that they regard as moving in a good direction.

The authors call for a unified federal approach that starts with disclosure requirements similar to those in some states and goes further. They propose features that let users clearly tell AIs from people throughout each interaction, perhaps through digital watermarking or identifiable video or speech markers. They argue that state-by-state rules would create a legal patchwork, and they stress that time is short. Closing with a nod to Stewart's legacy, they urge readers to reject Picard's position on AI personhood, ending with his phrase "Make it so."

Articles.Title: Captain Picard Was Wrong About AI Personhood

stories.Headline: Guest Editorial: Long Island’s AI Grants Should Buy Results, Not Just Subscriptions
stories.Summary:
Forty-nine Long Island business owners recently finished an intensive artificial intelligence training program, and each received a $5,000 grant to put a plan into practice. The LIA-AI Growth Academy was run by the Long Island Association Foundation and Stony Brook University, with funding from Google.org. The five-month program covered uses of AI for marketing, customer relationships, finance, and productivity. The first class celebrated its completion at Stony Brook on September 24.

The author argues that the next question is what will actually change in those businesses, and that grants should buy measurable results rather than software subscriptions. He warns that a company can buy a chatbot and write some marketing posts while customers still wait for answers and invoices still need the same corrections. Mistakes such as a misplaced price quote or a wrong appointment detail can erase any time saved. He suggests choosing one recurring task, recording its current time and error rate, and then testing an AI-assisted version for a few weeks.

He stresses that the time spent checking machine output belongs on the scorecard. The author, Dr. Gleb Tsipursky, is a behavioral scientist and CEO of Disaster Avoidance Experts, and he wrote the piece as a guest editorial in The South Shore Press. He cites a May 2026 Census Bureau analysis that found fewer than 20% of firms with four or fewer employees reported using AI, compared with 37% of firms employing at least 250 people. He notes that these figures measure reported use rather than profitable integration.

He also suggests the program publish voluntary, aggregated results at 30, 60, and 90 days, covering redesigned tasks, staff time recovered, error rates, and owners' views on customer value. The editorial does not report any decision by the program to publish such results, so whether the academy adopts the proposal remains unclear. It also does not describe the specific businesses in the cohort or their outcomes so far. The author's examples of a home-services operator, a retailer, and a professional-services firm are presented as illustrations rather than findings about participants.

Articles.Title: Guest Editorial: Long Island’s AI Grants Should Buy Results, Not Just Subscriptions

stories.Headline: Scammers are using AI-generated photos to demand ransom for lost pets
stories.Summary:
Criminals are using artificial intelligence to fake images of missing or injured pets and then demanding money for their supposed return. According to a NewsNation report published on November 7, 2026, scammers monitor social media posts about lost animals, take the photos owners share publicly, and alter them with AI so the pet appears found, hurt, or under veterinary care. They then contact the owners, ask for large payments, and threaten to kill or euthanize the animal if the money is not sent. Some scammers have also pretended to be police officers or shelter staff to make their claims seem real.

One example in the reporting involved a California woman who received a doctored image of her missing dog in May, along with a message saying the dog needed emergency surgery at a San Jose animal shelter. The scammer demanded money to continue treatment and warned the dog would be put down. When she contacted the shelter, staff confirmed the animal was not there, and the city's Animal Care and Services department issued a warning about the scheme. The shelter said scammers were using public lost pet posts and AI-generated content to create false urgency. The same pattern has appeared in the United Kingdom, where the BBC reported cases involving missing cats.

In one UK case, Cam Chauhan received a message months after her cat went missing demanding a £200 Apple gift card, along with a picture that seemed to show him in a garden. When she tried to set up a meeting place, the sender refused to proceed until she paid, and she recognized the scam, though her cat is still missing.
