In another, Sarah Robinson was contacted by someone with a convincing image of her cat who grew vague about the animal's location and then demanded £40,000, close to $54,000, through a money transfer link. When she refused, the sender threatened to kill the cat. Mashable, citing the same BBC reporting, said the scammers often prefer gift cards because those payments cannot be reversed.

The Federal Trade Commission advises pet owners to be wary of anyone who requests unusual payment methods in exchange for an animal or treatment. Owners are urged to request a live video call or a current video showing a distinctive feature, to ask questions about details a stranger could not learn from public photos, and to contact shelters, clinics, or police using independently verified phone numbers. Experts also warn never to send gift cards, cryptocurrency, or wire transfers to someone claiming they need money to return a pet, and to meet in a public place when possible. Suspected scams can be reported at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Articles.Title: Scammers are using AI-generated photos to demand ransom for lost pets

stories.Headline: The AI Selloff Just Got Messy. Here’s 3 Ways It Can Resolve (NYSEARCA:SPY)
stories.Summary:
The AI trade has sold off sharply, and the Seeking Alpha analysis by Amrita Roy, published on November 7, 2026, describes the decline as a bloodbath in AI-linked stocks. The article notes that the S&P 500 is down just 3.7% since October 1, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF, SMH, has fallen close to 25% over the same stretch. It says semiconductors suffered a particularly hard week shortly before publication. The piece frames the selloff as the central event of the moment for investors tracking the sector.

According to the author, the decline is driven by macro fears about credit risk tied to AI and the possibility of delays at data centers, following a Democratic sweep of Congress. The author argues these concerns are not the result of weakening fundamentals. The article says underlying demand for computing power and AI infrastructure remains robust, with hyperscaler cloud growth accelerating and hardware shortages persisting. It adds that the sell-off has produced steep discounts in high-quality AI stocks.

Roy, who manages a concentrated portfolio focused on AI infrastructure, says she is taking a nimble approach by expanding positions in top AI names while keeping liquidity. She expects the selloff to resolve in one of three ways, though the article's summary and excerpted text do not spell out those three scenarios in full. The author discloses long positions in a number of the stocks she discusses, including Amazon, Meta, Micron and Palantir. The piece is an opinion article, and Seeking Alpha notes that its analysts are third-party authors whose views may not reflect those of the platform.

Articles.Title: The AI Selloff Just Got Messy. Here’s 3 Ways It Can Resolve (NYSEARCA:SPY)

stories.Headline: What Is Digital Realty Trust (DLR) Signaling With Its Global AI Infrastructure Push?
stories.Summary:
Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR) has taken a significant equity stake in Australian data centre operator NextDC, alongside Goodman Group. The company is also extending its Innovation Lab network into Latin America, with the first facility focused on AI infrastructure use cases. Management plans further Innovation Lab locations in Singapore and Johannesburg to widen access to AI-ready data centre environments. The article is dated November 7, 2026, and was published by Simply Wall St on Yahoo Finance Singapore. The moves were reported as part of the company's broader AI infrastructure push.

The article does not spell out the size of the NextDC stake or the timing of the Latin American facility's opening. It describes Digital Realty as a US-based Specialized REIT with a market cap of about $67.2 billion, focused on data centres, colocation and interconnection services for enterprise customers. The piece argues that the NextDC stake and the São Paulo lab point in the same direction, with the company relying more on partners and testbed capacity rather than only building new capacity on its own balance sheet. It also cites a US$1.9 billion signed backlog and a 1.4 GW development pipeline. The author suggests that investors watch for growth in contracted AI-related bookings and higher utilization of high-density, liquid-cooled racks.

The article is produced with the assistance of AI automation and is written as general commentary rather than investment advice. Simply Wall St, the source of the analysis, states that it holds no position in the stocks it discusses. The piece notes that its analysis may not reflect the latest company announcements. The articles provided do not describe what happens next beyond the planned Singapore and Johannesburg labs.

Articles.Title: What Is Digital Realty Trust (DLR) Signaling With Its Global AI Infrastructure Push?

stories.Headline: SoundHound AI: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
stories.Summary:
SoundHound AI announced on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on November 5, 2026, that it expects to reach sustainable profitability within the second half of 2027. The company is moving away from lumpy upfront software license fees toward steady hosted subscriptions, and it is also cutting operating expenses across the business. Management described these changes as central to its plan for more predictable results. The call was reported by The Motley Fool on November 7, 2026, in an article that highlighted three takeaways from the call.

The first change involves its enterprise platform, OASYS, which runs software agents across voice and text. Management said it is using OASYS to turn single-point customer commitments into steady annualized recurring revenue by offering it as a hosted service. The company also said that OASYS's self-learning feature allows it to structure deals as hosted solutions while still securing long-term customer commitments. Management further said it is trimming at least $120 million in costs by integrating recent acquisitions, eliminating duplicate corporate functions, optimizing cloud spending, and dropping unprofitable contracts. Chief Financial Officer John Collins said the company expects positive adjusted EBITDA within the second half of 2027, even at the low end of its revenue guidance.

Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder Keyvan Mohajer said the company is replacing external AI models with its own technology to reduce computing costs. He said SoundHound has already moved hundreds of customers to this architecture, and that the change is improving accuracy and latency while cutting model costs by more than an order of magnitude. Mohajer also said the company has been non-renewing and exiting certain negative gross margin contracts inherited from prior acquisitions. Collins said that starting in 2027, adjusted EBITDA will be a regular part of the company's guidance. Quarterly revenue grew 48 percent year over year to a record $62.4 million, according to the article.

The article places these moves in the context of the company's structural advantages, including more than 800 patents and proprietary models that it says reduce its reliance on third-party vendor fees. Management says it is watching pricing discipline and the transition of customers to hosted services as key drivers of long-term value. The article also carried a promotional section urging readers to consider other stocks, which it said SoundHound AI was not among. The articles provided do not describe further steps beyond the stated 2027 profitability target.

Articles.Title: SoundHound AI: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

stories.Headline: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding
stories.Summary:
Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents, and says thousands of its engineers use it. The plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes any code, and then fresh subagents with no conversation history attack that spec. The stated goal is to catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file rather than in a pull request. The package includes 7 skills, 9 reviewer personas, 6 brainstorm lenses and 5 review stages, and it carries no model weights because the agent supplies the language model.

The plugin is an Apache 2.0 collection of skills, reviewer personas and document standards, not a new language model. It runs on any harness that can spawn fresh subagents, including Antigravity, Claude Code version 2.1.271 or later, Claude Cowork, Codex and ChatGPT, and it uses your existing model quota. No accuracy benchmark has been published, so the evidence offered is adoption and end-to-end harness test runs. The method traces to Dave Rensin's essay on elephants and goldfish, and the Google Open Source blog frames it as a fix for AI "slop" and session context collapse. The README says it is not an officially supported Google product.

The workflow splits work between a long-running session, called the Elephant, and stateless subagents, called Goldfish. The Elephant holds project context and drafts the spec without writing code, while each Goldfish reads only the draft and the files it references. The brainstorm command runs a six-lens Goldfish swarm covering YAGNI, token cost, UX, migration, observability and technical debt, and the draft command turns the brief into a design document. A drift-report command later compares code with the spec, and the docs recommend running it weekly. A five-stage Goldfish review then runs an initial zoom-out, a comprehension test, a critic review, an intermediate zoom-out and an implementation-readiness check, with each stage allowing at most one re-audit.

Responsibility for the design rests with the human developer, who resolves trade-offs and approves the design, while Google published the plugin under its open-source program. Among the test results, Codex 0.163.0 completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers in order and passed two live tests in 573.13 seconds, and the Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 run ran 16 native reviewers. The Claude Cowork run stopped after stages five through seven because of a usage limit, and an open issue, number 237, reports that AGENTS.md content leaks into Codex reviewers. The published comparison places EGM beside GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro Specs and Superpowers, and the main cost flagged is heavy token use along with unverified isolation on some hosts.

Articles.Title: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding

stories.Headline: How AI is changing holiday shopping and what advertisers need to know
stories.Summary:
The article is a Stacker piece distributed by abc17news.com on November 7, 2026, written for elk Marketing, and it explains how AI tools are changing the way holiday shoppers find and choose gifts. It reports that Americans spent $257.8 billion online during November and December 2025, according to Adobe, and argues that brands now need to think about how they enter an AI-generated shortlist before a shopper ever sees an advertisement. Shoppers can browse products, look for inspiration on social media and from reviews, or ask an AI tool for tailored suggestions and follow-up comparisons. The piece also notes that a strong search ranking does not guarantee a place in those AI answers.

The article points to several changes advertisers should prepare for. Pew Research Center found, in a study of 900 U.S. adults' March 2025 browsing, that traditional Google results drew clicks on 8% of visits when AI summaries appeared, compared with 15% without them, though the authors of the piece caution that the study was not shopping-specific and cannot prove cause and effect. OpenAI says its shopping results are chosen independently of advertising, drawing on shopper preferences, prices, product descriptions and reviews, so a larger ad budget alone cannot secure a recommendation. Meta says its Muse assistant can make purchases with user approval and has announced retail connections with Walmart and Best Buy, while Amazon lets customers track packages through Alexa. Adobe also measured a 693.4% annual increase in clicks from AI tools to retail sites during the 2025 holidays, a figure that counts clicks, not every purchase AI influenced.

The article advises brands to keep product data accurate across websites, shopping feeds and structured data, since outdated prices or missing delivery details can keep listings from appearing. It recommends clear product explanations, consistent brand information and credible outside reviews, and it warns against mass-produced content and promises of guaranteed AI rankings. Google's guidance, cited in the piece, stresses accessible pages and useful original content. The author frames these steps as a way to prepare without betting on one future, since the reach of personalization and automated purchasing remains uncertain. The piece concludes that AI is becoming part of the path to purchase, and that paid, organic and AI discovery should be planned and measured together.

Articles.Title: How AI is changing holiday shopping and what advertisers need to know

stories.Headline: GCC investors favour AI-assisted wealth advice over full automation, Avloq report finds
stories.Summary:
Avaloq, a Swiss banking technology provider headquartered in Zurich, has released its Wealth Insights 2026 report, which finds that investors across the Gulf Cooperation Council are open to artificial intelligence in wealth management but prefer human involvement in decisions. The report was covered by Arab News on November 7, 2026, and it draws on responses from GCC investors about how they want AI used with their money. Avaloq works with more than 170 institutions across 35 markets, supporting banking operations, portfolio management and digital services. Its managing director for the Middle East, Africa and India, Akash Anand, presented the findings and the company's view of where the sector is heading. The findings suggest that the technology will be welcomed most when it supports advisers rather than replacing them.

Anand said AI can ease one of the industry's persistent problems, which is limited adviser capacity. By reducing administrative tasks, AI would free advisers to spend more time with clients and serve a growing investor base. He added that the technology could support more tailored investment offers and widen access to asset classes that have mostly been open to wealthier clients, including private equity. He said investors could gain access to a broader range of opportunities, including more targeted products for the mass-affluent segment. Such changes would require banks and wealth managers to adopt and implement AI carefully.

According to the report, 67 percent of GCC investors are comfortable with their bank or wealth manager using AI, but they clearly prefer AI-assisted services over fully automated ones. For product recommendations, 54 percent are comfortable with AI-assisted advice, compared with 18 percent for fully automated recommendations, and 28 percent would prefer no AI involvement at all. The report also shows growing interest in digital assets, with 64 percent of respondents already holding them and 87 percent of those who do not saying they would consider investing if offered through a traditional bank or wealth manager. Anand observed that many investors still want the security, advice and established relationship that come with managing wealth through a bank.

Anand expects the GCC wealth management industry to become more competitive over the next five years, with regional institutions challenging established international players. He anticipates a stronger local industry emerging in that period. The article places these views within Saudi Arabia's broader financial development, where AI could help banks expand wealth services and improve efficiency. The report's findings point toward a market in which banks compete on a blend of technology and personal advice.

Articles.Title: GCC investors favour AI-assisted wealth advice over full automation, Avloq report finds

stories.Headline: S&P 500 Price Forecast: Strong Jobs Data Tests Rebound After AI Rout
stories.Summary:
The S&P 500 rebounded on Friday, November 6, 2026, after a sharp sell-off on Thursday driven by artificial intelligence concerns. The index had fallen to about 7,350 and closed below the key support level of 7,450, erasing the gains made after the US midterm elections. Chip stocks led the reversal, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rising more than 4% on Friday after plunging over 12% the day before. Even so, the market remains under pressure as traders weigh the strength of recent economic data.

Strong US jobs data for October showed employers adding 165,000 jobs, up from 60,000 in September, while the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% in October, and the US dollar index rallied after the release. The article says these figures lifted expectations of a December rate hike to 80%, complicating the equity recovery. The ISM Services PMI eased to 54.5 in October from 54.9 in September, though it still signals growth, and its prices index stayed high at 73. Investors also face uncertainty over possible tighter scrutiny of data center construction after Democratic gains in Congress and key states, which could slow demand for chips, power and equipment.

The article attributes the market's concerns to the AI-driven sell-off and to the policy uncertainty surrounding data centers, without naming any official who spoke on these matters. It notes that Nvidia fell more than 9% on Thursday, and that the semiconductor index has dropped more than 25% from its October 2026 peak. Oil prices also weigh on sentiment, as hopes of de-escalation in the Middle East compete with the risk of supply disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz that could revive inflation fears. On the technical side, the author says buyers must reclaim 7,450 to strengthen the recovery, with 7,325 as the next key level below. A break above 7,450 could open the way toward 7,800, while a drop below 7,325 could deepen the correction.

Articles.Title: S&P 500 Price Forecast: Strong Jobs Data Tests Rebound After AI Rout

stories.Headline: The market needed AI to come back strong. That’s not happening.
stories.Summary:
Democrats swept Tuesday's elections and took over leadership of both houses of Congress, prompting a sharp rally in U.S. stocks, a pullback in Treasury yields, and a steep drop in oil prices. The post-election surge delivered the largest one-day gain for the Dow Jones Industrial Average since April 9, 2025, and removed several obstacles that could have fueled a year-end rally. However, by Thursday the mood had reversed, as the Nasdaq Composite plunged more than 1,300 points and entered correction territory. The article reports that the reversal centers on the artificial intelligence investment theme, which is now viewed as the most uncertain part of the outlook.

Investors are weighing whether the election will meaningfully change the fundamentals behind the AI buildout, particularly data-center construction. Democrats won major gubernatorial races in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, and Pennsylvania, and the article says nearly every major local ballot measure opposing data centers won or was winning, with North Dakota the only exception. Michael Cembalest of J.P. Morgan Asset Management warned that this could put a quarter of next year's buildout and all of the 96 gigawatts of capacity expected for 2028 into question. The potential conditions include requiring data centers to pay grid costs, ending tax incentives, and banning non-disclosure agreements during permitting.

The article attributes the concern to several analysts and strategists. Seema Shah of Principal Asset Management said attention should soon return to Fed policy, corporate earnings, and the AI boom, and that the election is unlikely to set the medium-term direction unless it changes those fundamentals. Jonas Goltermann of Capital Economics said investors had recently reacted negatively to news of higher tech capital spending, so a possible enforced slowdown could be seen as good news. Jakub Rochlitz of eToro said the market is repricing growth expectations across sectors, noting that recoveries have not followed the drops and that selling is spreading.

The selloff has been severe. Nvidia fell 9.2% to $181.64, entering a bear market in less than a month for a stock worth $4.5 trillion, and the PHLX Semiconductor index dropped 11% on the day. The Magnificent Seven index fell 5% Thursday, shedding more than $1 trillion and sitting 10% below its October 13 high, while the Cboe Volatility Index jumped nearly 50% to 24.47. The article says it remains unclear whether the sell-off signals the coming eight weeks of trading or is a short-term reaction, but it concludes that the AI buildout, once central to growth and profit projections, is now an open question.

Articles.Title: The market needed AI to come back strong. That’s not happening.

stories.Headline: Data centre bosses cash in on India's AI and cloud expansion with handsome pay packages
stories.Summary:
Mint reported on November 7, 2026, that the chief executives of India's leading data centre companies are earning rising pay packages as the sector grows. The article, written by Yadukrishna C S and Jas Bardia, drew on financial reports from the country's top operators. Its central finding is that as these firms recorded higher revenues, their chiefs were rewarded handsomely. Manoj Paul, managing director of Equinix's Indian operations, topped the list with annual pay of ₹5.91 crore, although that figure was down 13% from FY24. Ashish Arora, chief executive of Nxtra by Airtel, has seen his pay rise roughly in step with the company's earnings growth since he joined in August 2022.

His salary reached ₹3.1 crore in August 2026, a compounded annual growth rate of nearly 10% over four years, while Nxtra's revenue grew at a compound rate of 15% to ₹2,434 crore. Piyush Somani, chairman and managing director of ESDS Software Solution, saw his net pay more than double from ₹83.8 lakh in FY24 to ₹1.8 crore in FY26. Over the same period, his firm's revenue rose 65% to ₹472.2 crore. Some executives are also paid in equity, with Arora granted 6,186 stock options in FY25 according to the company's annual report, though the filing did not establish their eventual cash value.

The article ties these packages to the scale of the sector's growth. India's data centre industry, valued at $5.5 billion, is entering its biggest expansion phase yet, fuelled by demand from cloud and artificial intelligence companies. Indian business houses, standalone operators and large technology firms have committed cumulative investments above $250 billion over the past 12 months. Amit Chandra, vice president at HDFC Securities, told Mint that pay is linked to performance, and that bosses appear to be rewarded for delivering capacity on time as demand rises.

Four companies, Yotta Data Services, NTT India, STT Global Data Centres and CtrlS Datacenters, did not disclose individual salaries, and several others did not respond to Mint's queries before publication. Mint's research also compared these figures with India's IT services sector, where the top executives at the 10 largest outsourcers earned between ₹27 crore and ₹390 crore in FY26, mostly through stock options. Kunal Bajaj, an equity research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities, attributed the gap to the greater size and responsibility of IT firms, but expected it to narrow as data centre operators keep growing at double-digit rates. The article notes that the industry is still in its building and expansion phases, and that pay levels are likely to keep rising alongside the sector's growth.

Articles.Title: Data centre bosses cash in on India's AI and cloud expansion with handsome pay packages

stories.Headline: Motorola Signature 27 launched: 200MP camera, Gemini AI, 7,000mAh battery and GrapheneOS support — what’s new?
stories.Summary:
Motorola has launched the Signature 27, its newest flagship smartphone, with the company announcing it on Thursday, November 5. The device has been revealed for global markets and is described as the company's most advanced smartphone so far. It pairs a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto camera with Google's Gemini AI features, a high-brightness display and a 7,000mAh battery. Motorola also says it will be the first of its phones to support GrapheneOS, a security-focused open-source operating system. The phone's camera system uses four lenses, including a 50MP Sony LYTIA L910 primary sensor, a 200MP periscope telephoto lens offering 100x Super Zoom, a 50MP ultrawide and a 50MP front camera.

Motorola says the camera system earned a DXOMARK Gold Label for imaging quality. The display is an Extreme AMOLED Duo panel with peak brightness of up to 12,000 nits. Inside, the phone runs on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 platform, and its battery is 35% larger than the previous generation, with 90W wired and 50W wireless charging. Motorola is positioning the device as an AI-focused product, and the company says it is designed for Gemini Intelligence. Its own tools include Rambler, which turns spoken words into tidy written messages, and Sign-to-Text, which uses the front camera to translate American Sign Language into written English in real time.

The phone also supports Google's Gemini Omni for video creation and editing and Lyria for generating soundtracks. The GrapheneOS support is being developed in partnership with the GrapheneOS Foundation. Motorola said the Signature 27 will reach markets worldwide in the coming months, with a starting recommended retail price of $1,599. The company has not yet announced pricing or availability for India. The launch places the device among the premium options in the company's lineup, and the articles do not describe any further rollout timeline beyond the coming months.

Articles.Title: Motorola Signature 27 launched: 200MP camera, Gemini AI, 7,000mAh battery and GrapheneOS support — what’s new?

stories.Headline: China’s AI models, led by Kimi, rule open-source enterprise spending
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models, led by Moonshot AI's Kimi family, accounted for nearly nine-tenths of estimated global enterprise spending on open-source systems, according to a new study released this week. The report came from Silicon Valley venture capital firm Menlo Ventures. Its figures show that Chinese systems made up 89 per cent of global enterprise spending on open-source models. Kimi alone held a 61 per cent share, ahead of DeepSeek at 15 per cent and Z.ai's GLM series at 11 per cent.

Meta Platforms' Llama series, the leading Western offering in the open-source category, accounted for just 7 per cent of that enterprise spending. The study also noted that proprietary US rivals still capture the vast majority of overall AI revenue. Open-source models are free to download and modify, and companies that use them typically pay for hosting, integration or support. The distinction matters because the open-source category is small compared with spending on proprietary models. The findings therefore describe a narrow slice of the market rather than the industry as a whole.

Menlo Ventures released the report, and the article attributes its findings to that firm's analysis of enterprise spending. The article does not include a statement from Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, Z.ai or Meta responding to the figures. It also does not describe any changes to pricing, regulation or licensing tied to the study. The study is presented as a snapshot of spending patterns rather than a policy action. No further developments are reported in the article.

Articles.Title: China’s AI models, led by Kimi, rule open-source enterprise spending

stories.Headline: Chinese university stops using AI to spot absent-minded students after outcry
stories.Summary:
Nanjing University, a top institution in Jiangsu province in eastern China, has stopped using a controversial feature of its AI-powered classroom tracking system after a fierce public backlash. The university had told students it would use its upgraded "smart classroom" system to record full attendance over a one-week period, according to Chinese media reports from Wednesday. Outrage grew when leaked screenshots appeared to show the software at work, pairing live classroom footage with real-time data on late arrivals, attendance and a "head-up rate" meant to gauge attentiveness. The images spread widely online and sparked heated debate about campus privacy, the ethics of algorithmic surveillance and the limits on AI monitoring. The report describes the rollback as following that public reaction.

The articles indicate that the feature in question was the tracking of students' attentiveness and attendance across the one-week period announced by the university. The "head-up rate" measure, which the leaked images suggested was used to map how attentive students were, is the element that drew the most criticism. The available reporting does not give the exact date the rollback took effect or describe any replacement arrangement for attendance. It also does not say how many students were affected or how the system's data was stored.

The article does not give a detailed account of the university's own explanation for the rollback, so no direct statement from university officials is set out here. The reporting attributes the change to the public outcry that followed the leaked images. The leaked screenshots themselves were described as purportedly coming from the software in use, which means their authenticity is not confirmed in the report. Students and the wider public responded strongly, and the report frames the episode as part of a broader debate over AI monitoring.

The story is set against growing public discussion in China about how far artificial intelligence should reach into everyday life, including schools and universities. The articles do not say whether other institutions are reviewing similar systems or whether regulators have taken any action. Beyond the rollback, the report does not describe what the university plans next for its smart classroom system. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Chinese university stops using AI to spot absent-minded students after outcry

stories.Headline: Meta launches its Muse AI agent in Mexico, a first for the Latin American market
stories.Summary:
Meta has made its Muse AI agent available in Mexico, making the country the first in Latin America to receive the tool. Meta's Mexico country manager, Marco Casarin, announced the launch in a LinkedIn post, and the agent is now offered in Spanish. Muse is available to users over 18 through iOS, Android and muse.ai. Its compatibility with AI glasses and its availability through WhatsApp are planned for later. According to Casarin, Muse goes beyond answering questions, since users state a goal and the agent works out a plan and carries it forward on its own.

He said it can connect to a user's email, calendar, messages and Instagram, as well as to other apps and services, all under the user's control. The first connectors in Mexico will cover retail, credit and lending, travel, car rental, entertainment and food delivery. Brands named by Casarin include Cinépolis, Coppel, Despegar, Kavak, Liverpool and Rappi, which would let users buy movie tickets, find cars, plan trips and compare deals. Casarin stressed that the user keeps control, deciding what Muse can access and authorizing each action before it happens.

The article's own caution is that giving an AI agent access to this information means sharing more details about one's life, and once that data is obtained it cannot be retrieved. It also notes that Meta's past handling of user data, as Fast Company has pointed out, makes its privacy promises harder to accept. The launch comes as part of Meta's wider push to bring AI agents to users, and the article describes these systems as more adaptable than traditional chatbots and large language models because they draw on data and analytics tools to reason through complex tasks. The article does not say when the additional connectors or device integrations will arrive beyond the stated plans, nor does it report any regulatory response in Mexico.

Articles.Title: Meta launches its Muse AI agent in Mexico, a first for the Latin American market

stories.Headline: Microsoft Reduces Neocloud Partnerships Amid AI Infrastructure Stock Declines
stories.Summary:
Microsoft is reportedly cutting back its reliance on third-party AI cloud providers, known as neoclouds, and shifting priority toward its own data centers. CNBC reported on Friday, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Microsoft is still deciding which neocloud providers to drop and had decided against renewing an Oracle deal. Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The move comes as shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have each fallen roughly 45% over the past month, despite gains on Friday.

Neocloud providers rent out graphics processing units, or GPUs, for AI workloads, and Microsoft began using them after the launch of ChatGPT in 2022 drove a surge in demand. CoreWeave disclosed in a March 2025 regulatory filing that Microsoft generated 62% of its revenue in 2024. Microsoft has already withdrawn from an Nscale site in England, and its U.K. and Ireland CEO, Darren Hardman, said in October that Nscale's electricity access was behind that decision. The Financial Times reported this week that Microsoft will not renew a contract with Nscale in Texas. Construction delays at IREN's site in Childress, Texas, reportedly prompted Microsoft to postpone about $5 billion in planned spending, according to The Information.

Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said in October that some GPU-related cloud contracts had been delayed until the first half of 2027, which slowed Azure growth. The company's capital expenditures and finance leases reached $45.2 billion last quarter. IREN said a networking upgrade requested by a customer pushed back the operation of capacity it delivered in August until January or February. Research firm Aterio's satellite analysis also indicates possible delays at IREN's Childress site and at Nebius's project in Vineland, New Jersey, where about 140 megawatts of capacity could slip until 2027. Higher interest rates and concerns over data center expansion after the midterm elections have added to investor anxiety about these companies' dependence on borrowing.

IREN reported AI revenue of $200 million, more than double the previous level, and forecasts about $15 billion in capital spending for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. The company is still looking for financing to cover roughly $6 billion of that amount. Microsoft's market capitalization is about $3.94 trillion, and its shares have traded between $349.20 and $559.15 over the past 52 weeks. The articles do not say which neocloud providers Microsoft will ultimately drop, and Microsoft has not confirmed the reported changes.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Reduces Neocloud Partnerships Amid AI Infrastructure Stock Declines

stories.Headline: Meta AI will forget less and give up less often with new upgrade
stories.Summary:
Meta has upgraded the models that power its Muse agent and Meta AI, borrowing two capabilities from its frontier Muse Wonder model. The company said in a blog post that the specialised models would begin rolling out to Muse and Meta AI users on Friday, November 7, 2026. The update is aimed at making AI assistants that can remember important details from past conversations and keep working when a task runs into trouble. Meta describes the goal as moving its AI beyond answering questions toward helping users get things done. Subscribers can still use Muse Wonder itself for more demanding tasks.

The first addition, which Meta calls Active Memory, lets assistants recall useful information from earlier chats instead of treating each conversation as a fresh start. The models can tell temporary details apart from information that stays relevant over time, which matters for work that spans several days, such as planning a trip. Meta says the models show a 2.4 times reduction in forgetting critical information. In its internal evaluation, they used important context correctly in 90 per cent of tasks, up from 76 per cent previously. The second capability, Active Focus, is meant to help the AI keep going when something fails, such as a broken website or a stuck booking.

Meta says the models show a 67 per cent improvement in completing everyday tasks when unexpected problems arise. Mark Zuckerberg announced the upgrade on X, describing the models as "2.4x less likely to forget critical info" and "67 per cent better at self correcting and completing everyday tasks." Meta's blog post, as reported, presents these figures as results from its own testing rather than independent verification. The company also says the models are better at deciding when to work independently and when to ask users for help, and at adapting to corrections made mid-task.

Meta's broader approach is to use Muse Wonder to train specialised models for everyday work instead of giving every user its most expensive frontier model. The company says the goal is to bring "even more capable superintelligence" to more people. Muse is designed to act as a personal agent, and Meta AI is available across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. The article notes that the real test will be whether these upgrades make the assistants genuinely more useful in daily life, a question the reported figures alone cannot settle.

Articles.Title: Meta AI will forget less and give up less often with new upgrade

stories.Headline: A gun-control group has plans for safe chatting with AI
stories.Summary:
Everytown for Gun Safety, one of the most influential gun-control organizations in the country, has reportedly made plans for how it will chat safely with artificial intelligence. The article, published by the Washington Examiner on November 7, 2026, centers on this initiative. It is the only detail the piece offers about the plans themselves, so the reporting leaves much unexplained. The article does not lay out what the chatting would involve or what safeguards would be used. Everytown was founded in 2014 through the merger of Mayors Against Illegal Guns and Moms Demand Action.

Over the past decade it has used political spending, litigation, research, and lobbying to push for stricter firearms laws. The article names campaigns for expanded background checks, restrictions on certain firearms, and laws that let courts temporarily remove guns from people deemed dangerous. The article does not say whether the AI plans connect to any of these efforts. The article does not identify any specific person at Everytown who spoke about the plans, and it does not quote a spokesperson. It also does not describe any response from the organization, from AI companies, or from critics.

Without those statements, the piece cannot tell readers who is responsible for the plans or what they have said about them. Beyond the organization's background, the article offers little context about the plans' timing or scope. It does not say whether the plans are underway, how they would be carried out, or what the next steps would be. Readers seeking those details will need further reporting, and the article itself does not indicate what comes next.

Articles.Title: A gun-control group has plans for safe chatting with AI - Washington Examiner

stories.Headline: CalPrivacy expresses support for privacy legislation targeting AI training
stories.Summary:
California's privacy agency said on November 6, 2026 that it would be willing to back privacy legislation aimed at restricting the use of personal data for artificial intelligence training. The statement came from the agency as it explores which legislative topics to sponsor or support in the coming year. The reporting, published by MLex and written by Xu Yuan, presents this as a stance still under consideration rather than a finished proposal. The articles give no details of a specific bill, its text, or its timeline. The agency's position signals interest in limiting how personal information may feed into AI systems during training.

As described, the willingness to support such rules is conditional on the agency's broader legislative planning for the year ahead. The articles do not specify any numbers, deadlines, penalties, or affected categories of data. They also do not name any lawmaker or bill that would carry the measure forward. The statement was attributed to California's privacy agency, the body that oversees the state's privacy rules. The reporting paraphrases the agency's comments rather than quoting specific language at length.

It describes the agency as considering which topics to sponsor or endorse, with AI training data now among them. No further remarks from individual officials appear in the articles. The context is that AI training on personal data has become a focus of privacy concern, though the articles themselves do not elaborate on specific incidents or prior rules. What happens next is not spelled out in the reporting. Any actual legislation would depend on the agency's selection process and on the state's legislative calendar, neither of which the articles describe.

Articles.Title: CalPrivacy expresses support for privacy legislation targeting AI training - MLex

stories.Headline: Docusign modernizes its eSignature data platform and builds an AI-ready future with Azure SQL
stories.Summary:
Docusign, the electronic signature company, has modernized its core eSignature data platform by moving it onto Microsoft Azure, according to a Microsoft customer story published on November 7, 2026. The work was driven by a 308 TB on-premises SQL Server database, called DocusignDB, which had reached a single-instance ceiling and could no longer scale efficiently. Docusign worked with Microsoft SQL Engineering to split this database across several Azure SQL services without rewriting the application. The company says the platform serves more than 1.9 million customers and a billion people in 180 countries.

The modernization required breaking the monolithic database into smaller parts, using a mix of custom Azure SQL configurations, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure SQL virtual machines, and Azure SQL Database Hyperscale. Docusign migrated nearly 200 million accounts across five global sites with zero rollbacks, according to the article. The database, which had more than 500 tables and 8,000 stored procedures, had been generating heavy input and output demand at its busiest site. Docusign said a one-to-one migration would have carried the same limits forward, while moving accounts one at a time would have added unacceptable cross-datacenter latency.

Josh Meier, Senior Principal Engineer at Docusign, said the database had begun approaching its practical capacity, with contention at the busiest site limiting throughput. Abhishek Chaturvedi, a Fellow at Docusign, said the aim was to match each Azure service to its workload rather than place every database on one service. He credited the team with moving the accounts while the eSignature service stayed live. Meier said the application can now stay stable while the data and infrastructure beneath it change in smaller steps.

The article reports that after a sub-five-minute site-level failover, storage tuning cut average read time by 5 milliseconds, and P99 latency for signing sessions dropped by over 3 seconds at the largest North American sites. Docusign validated the work with 35,000 test cases and more than 50 runbook rehearsals. The company plans to move more eSign services onto its Kubernetes-based platform and decommission its on-premises datacenters. The modernized Azure foundation is also meant to support AI features, including Docusign Iris, which powers its AI contract management platform.

Articles.Title: Docusign modernizes its eSignature data platform and builds an AI-ready future with Azure SQL

stories.Headline: Wall Street Already Has 10 Leveraged Anthropic ETFs Lined Up, and Half Bet Against It
stories.Summary:
Five issuers have filed prospectuses with the SEC for at least 10 leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, even though its stock has not yet been listed. As of November 6, 2026, the filings cover funds that aim to deliver 2x the daily move of the stock and funds that aim for -2x, so about half would rise when Anthropic falls. The article reports that Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on October 26 and amended it on November 2. The company plans to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, but it has not set a price range or a date.

The filings show that issuers are selling funds in both directions to attract traders on either side, which the article says reflects product design rather than a forecast. Expense ratios vary by issuer, with ProShares listing 0.95% net, Defiance 0.71% for its long fund, GraniteShares 1.33% for its long fund, Direxion 0.97% net for its bull fund, and Leverage Shares 0.75%. Direxion first filed on NYSE Arca on October 27 and moved to Nasdaq in an October 28 revision. Tradr pushed its effective date to November 12, and REX has a pair in a November 4 filing that is not yet effective.

The article attributes the filings to the issuers themselves, who are competing to claim tickers and assets before the stock trades. It explains that the first fund to list in a hot segment often collects most of the assets, and that filing early secures a place in line. The article also notes that an effective prospectus only passes paperwork, since ProShares' funds became effective November 6 yet its fund page says neither has launched. Inverse funds could matter early because borrowable shares of a new IPO are scarce, so a -2x fund gives bears an easier short position, which could add selling pressure in ANT's first weeks.

The article warns that daily resets cause multi-week returns to diverge sharply from twice the stock's move, and that choppy trading hurts both long and inverse funds. It estimates that at 90% volatility the Defiance long fund would be expected to lose 76% over a year even if the stock ended flat. Timing remains uncertain, with prediction-market odds of a listing before December 1 falling from about 80% to near 50% as AI stocks sold off. Anthropic had been targeting the week before Thanksgiving and could raise up to $100 billion, with unnamed sources discussing a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.3 trillion. None of the funds can trade until ANT does, and the article points to an amended S-1 with a price range as the next trigger to watch.

Articles.Title: Wall Street Already Has 10 Leveraged Anthropic ETFs Lined Up, and Half Bet Against It

stories.Headline: METR Estimates Anthropic’s AI Benchmark Improvement Rate at 1.9 Times Historical Pace
stories.Summary:
METR, an AI evaluation group, has estimated that Anthropic's AI benchmark improvement rate has sped up to about 1.9 times its earlier pace since October 2025. The estimate was published by TokenPost on November 7, 2026, and reporter Simon Yoon covered it. METR measured the new rate against the pace from March 2024 through October 2025, using a benchmark it calls AECI. The review examined an 11-week period running from August 12 to October 29.

To reach its findings, METR examined confidential data, interviewed Anthropic staff and reviewed proprietary performance metrics. According to the estimate, about 80% of the acceleration came from Anthropic's internal use of its models for research and development. Most of those gains came from models assisting human researchers rather than running processes fully on their own. The article says faster growth in training compute did not drive the increase. The assessment followed Anthropic's October 15 announcement that six METR employees would gain access to certain internal systems, equipment and office space through its safety review arrangement.

METR is the body that produced the estimate, and the article attributes the findings to it. The article does not include any direct statement from Anthropic about the estimate. The findings bear on concerns about recursive AI self-improvement, a process in which AI systems help develop later AI systems. The article notes that METR's estimate rests on one benchmark and a single 11-week evaluation period. It does not say whether METR plans further reviews or whether Anthropic will respond publicly.

Articles.Title: METR Estimates Anthropic’s AI Benchmark Improvement Rate at 1.9 Times Historical Pace

stories.Headline: Call for Applications: Microsoft AI Economy Institute Research Grants (Up to $75,000 in Grants)
stories.Summary:
Microsoft's AI Economy Institute (AIEI) has opened applications for the fourth cohort of its Senior Fellows Programme, which offers selected researchers a research grant of US$75,000 to study how artificial intelligence is changing work and economic opportunity. The call was published on November 7, 2026, by MSME Africa, and the institute, which was launched in 2025, supports independent research on AI's effects on productivity, labour markets, education and economic development. The fourth cohort's theme is "AI and Jobs: Designing for Augmented Work," and the call asks for proposals on how organisational choices decide whether AI complements human work, replaces certain tasks or creates new economic activity. Researchers may look at workflow design, team structures, governance, incentives, accountability and skills development.

Eligibility is open to researchers at accredited universities or research institutions worldwide. Principal Investigators and co-Principal Investigators must hold a PhD or an equivalent terminal degree such as an MD, JD or DrPH at the time of application. A proposal may name up to two Principal Investigators, but only one award is issued per selected proposal, and interdisciplinary teams are encouraged to apply if every Principal Investigator meets the requirements. Each selected proposal receives the US$75,000 grant along with one travel allowance for the in-person workshop: US$7,500 for awardees based in the United States, Canada or Mexico, and US$20,000 for those based elsewhere.

Applicants submit a biosketch, prepared in 11-point font, that includes a personal statement of no more than 300 words, a one-page professional summary, up to three contributions to science, and current research support with citation metrics such as the H-index, total citations and I-index. They also submit a project overview describing the research question, methods, expected contribution, policy relevance and up to three target academic journals. Selected fellows take part in bi-weekly virtual workshops, attend a multi-day in-person workshop with Microsoft experts and AIEI leadership, contribute a chapter to an edited trade book on the AI economy, and submit a manuscript to an open-access academic journal. Proposals go through the institute's application portal, and the official call guidelines are available on Microsoft's research website.

Articles.Title: Call for Applications: Microsoft AI Economy Institute Research Grants (Up to $75,000 in Grants)

stories.Headline: Companies must retain accountability as autonomous AI agents take on business decisions, say legal experts
stories.Summary:
Legal experts are urging companies to keep clear human accountability as they hand more business decisions to autonomous AI agents, which can approve transactions, place vendor orders and process financial decisions with limited human involvement. The call comes as enterprises move beyond AI-assisted tools, and it is backed by a global study from Tata Consultancy Services that covered 1,333 senior business and technology leaders across 25 countries and 12 industries. The study found that 84% of executives see productivity gains as the leading source of value from AI, yet only 10% of enterprises let AI agents make decisions without human approval across multiple functions, and just 9% have agents that can securely orchestrate workflows across enterprise applications. The gap between expectations and readiness is the focus of the discussion.

Experts say the deployment of such agents raises questions about liability, data protection, intellectual property rights and regulatory compliance. Malak Bhatt, Chamber Head at Chambers of Malak Bhatt, said autonomous agents do not dilute accountability because AI has no legal personality under Indian law, so contractual, tortious and regulatory liability would ordinarily fall on the enterprise deploying the technology. Bhatt recommended that companies inventory where agents are used, set approval thresholds, keep humans overseeing consequential decisions and maintain audit trails that can reconstruct how a decision was reached. Vendor agreements, he added, should cover data usage and training rights, performance warranties, incident reporting, audit access and indemnities, and compliance should be built in from the start, with attention to the Digital Personal Data Protection framework and to sectoral regulators such as the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India.

Dinesh Jotwani, Partner and Founder at Jotwani Associates, said agents are moving beyond routine tasks such as drafting emails to actions like transferring money, placing orders and approving loans. He noted that India has no single consolidated AI law, so such operations fall under existing rules, including the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. He said AI cannot assume contractual responsibility, so a business that lets an agent place an erroneous order cannot shift the liability onto the technology, and he warned of data protection penalties and consumer or product liability claims over faulty AI decisions such as unfair loan rejections. Companies are responding, he said, with spending limits, restricted access to sensitive information, human sign-off on high-risk decisions, tamper-proof records of prompts and actions, stronger indemnity clauses in vendor contracts and internal AI governance committees.

The TCS study ranks security, risk and governance above cost, speed and ease of implementation as the main considerations in enterprise AI decisions. It found that 90% of respondents see model independence as an important factor, 34% rate AI sovereignty requirements as a high or very high organisational risk, and 39% are still judging whether their AI initiatives create enough value relative to token and computing costs. Only 7% of respondents have organisation-wide plans for switching AI providers without disruption. Amit Kapur, Chief AI and Services Transformation Officer at TCS, said productivity is where enterprises currently see the greatest value from AI, with 84% of executives ranking it first and 10% reporting a revenue uplift.

Articles.Title: Companies must retain accountability as autonomous AI agents take on business decisions, say legal experts - ETLegalWorld.com

stories.Headline: State Farm scales governed AI to deliver enterprise business value with Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Platform
stories.Summary:
State Farm, one of the largest insurance and financial services companies in the United States, has been scaling governed AI capabilities using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Platform, as described in a Microsoft customer story published on November 7, 2026. The company, headquartered in Bloomington, Illinois, and employing about 65,000 people, sought a clear and enterprise-ready way to explore and build AI tools that could help employees work more efficiently. The effort is tied to its Human + Digital strategy and is supported by technologies including Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft Entra ID. Teams were already eager to build, but the company needed a path that turned isolated experiments into production-ready solutions. Rather than treating governance as an obstacle, State Farm used clear approval paths and close work with risk and compliance teams to help builders move ideas forward with confidence.

Training and collaboration shaped the rollout. State Farm ran hands-on workshops built on Microsoft-provided labs, adapted to its own governance requirements, with sessions that can reach up to 150 attendees. Engineering Manager Azsure Dorton described an approach in which people start by building for themselves, then for their team and department, before enterprise ideas take shape. The article reports that 41 builds have passed risk assessments and are in production, and that more than 3,000 AI agent identities exist within the Power Platform environment. Reusable catalog capabilities let teams share connectors and solutions, and one innovation sprint produced a reusable onboarding and offboarding solution combining Power Apps, Power Automate, and Copilot Studio.

Measurable results were reported in several areas. An HR policy agent built in Copilot Studio lets employees find answers about policies and benefits without contacting an HR representative, and within 30 days it became the second most-used agent at State Farm. The HR team has a roadmap of 12 more agents, and an underwriting agent helps underwriters and trainees search criteria that had been held in large manuals now stored in SharePoint Online. A translation workflow reduced turnaround for marketing materials between English and Spanish from 12 months to 24 hours. Dorton said the HR agent saved the department considerable time and helped employees find information on their own, and she said AI elevates employees' ability to do their jobs.

The company's next step is moving beyond knowledge-retrieval agents toward more complex, action-oriented or autonomous agents that can work across systems. State Farm plans build-a-thons focused on orchestration, approvals, and intelligent apps, and it is considering an AI-enabled capability to help potential employees understand the employee experience, with review and controls in place. Builders are also testing the Power Apps Vibe experience for rapid prototyping. Dorton said success would mean employees having personal agents and enterprise-scale agents that move across systems, and the article presents these plans as ongoing rather than final.

Articles.Title: State Farm scales governed AI to deliver enterprise business value with Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Platform

stories.Headline: IBM Ties AI Agent Governance to a Five-Year Tennis Deal and a Raised Cash Target - ad-hoc-news.de
stories.Summary:
IBM has extended its partnership with the United States Tennis Association by five years, a deal announced on 28 October that keeps the Armonk-based company as the official artificial intelligence and cloud partner of the US Open through 2031. The renewal came alongside a wider product push covering agent identity controls, quantum hardware and post-quantum cryptography. It also followed a refreshed financial outlook the company published on 21 October. On 27 October IBM unveiled enterprise features for identifying and governing AI agents, including tools for agent discovery, verified identities, access controls, and ways to assess how well those agents perform inside corporate systems. The company said several of these capabilities are now generally available, while others remain in preview.

The agent identity and administration focus had first been flagged about two weeks earlier at its TechXchange event. Confluent, an IBM-owned company, added updates to its Streamhouse architecture to keep the business data that agents and analytics rely on current. On the hardware side, IBM introduced a Quantum System Two in Chicago on a Friday, describing it as operational at the Hyde Park Labs site and its most advanced system available. It is IBM's first quantum machine in Illinois and runs on the Quantum-Nighthawk processor with 120 qubits. A day earlier IBM, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD launched a joint development platform for quantum error correction, with a first phase linking IBM quantum computers to the research centre's Umbra system, which uses AMD processors and graphics chips.

The effort supports the US Department of Energy's Quantum Genesis Mission, and IBM has also packaged IBM Quantum Safe as one suite to help enterprises manage their move to post-quantum cryptography. The financial backdrop came in third-quarter 2026 results published on 21 October, which reported revenue of $17.1 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.95. Management kept its full-year outlook for currency-adjusted revenue growth at 4% to 5%, but raised its free cash flow growth target so that the metric is now expected to rise by more than $1 billion year over year. Taken together, the sponsorship, governance tools and quantum launches show IBM pairing its AI and quantum ambitions with a stronger cash picture, though the articles do not say how these products will affect future sales.

Articles.Title: IBM Ties AI Agent Governance to a Five-Year Tennis Deal and a Raised Cash Target - ad-hoc-news.de

stories.Headline: In Case You Missed It: A.I./Data Center Articles - NewClips From Last Week - November 9 - PA Environment Digest Blog
stories.Summary:
PJM Interconnection filed a revised reliability backstop generation procurement proposal with FERC, according to the PA Environment Digest roundup posted on October 31, 2026. The grid operator wants to hold its next auction in March 2027 with a price cap of $555 per megawatt-day. The filing is PJM's revised proposal for procuring backstop generation to support reliability. The digest lists the filing among its A.I. and data center news clips from the week.

The proposal sets the next auction for March 2027 and caps the price at $555 per megawatt-day. Those figures come from the digest's summary of the filing. The digest does not say what else the revised proposal changes or what FERC has done with it. It also does not say when FERC might act on the filing.

PJM Interconnection is the grid operator that made the filing with FERC. The digest does not include any statement from PJM or from FERC about the proposal. It gives no explanation from either side for the revision or the price cap. No other details from the filing are reported in the digest.

The filing appears in a weekly roundup of articles and news clips on A.I. and data center issues. The digest does not say what happens next beyond the planned March 2027 auction. It does not report a schedule for FERC's review. More to follow.

Articles.Title: In Case You Missed It: A.I./Data Center Articles - NewClips From Last Week - November 9 - PA Environment Digest Blog

stories.Headline: Email to staff: Jensen Huang admits an affair, takes "full responsibility", and says he fell short of his duties to Nvidia's board, shareholders, and employees (Madison Mills/Axios)
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted in an email to staff that he had an affair, and the company's board said it would launch an independent investigation on Sunday. The admission came in a draft email to Nvidia employees that Axios obtained. Huang wrote that he owed his family and everyone at the company an apology, and he said he had been unfaithful to his wife. In the message, Huang took "full responsibility" for his conduct and said he had fallen short of his duties to Nvidia's employees, board, and shareholders.

He wrote that leading the company was the privilege of his life and that he was fully committed to it. The board said an independent committee, supported by outside counsel, will examine the matter. It also said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and it expressed confidence in Huang's leadership. The affair involved a woman that U.S. intelligence officials believed was a Chinese spy, according to The New York Times, which reported on Friday that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had warned top Trump administration officials about the relationship.

The Times reported that the woman, Alice Huang, had been recruited to seek information and potentially push for Nvidia's advanced chips to be made available in China. The story carries weight because Huang has been a prominent voice in Washington urging looser limits on AI chip sales to China, arguing that keeping American technology in that market strengthens U.S. competitiveness. Nvidia's public policy communications head, John Rizzo, said in a statement that the news would not slow the company and that Huang would keep leading Nvidia as CEO without interruption. The articles do not say what the outcome of the board's investigation will be or when it will report its findings.

Articles.Title: Email to staff: Jensen Huang admits an affair, takes "full responsibility", and says he fell short of his duties to Nvidia's board, shareholders, and employees (Madison Mills/Axios)

stories.Headline: Hybrid AI Model Predicts Postoperative Lung Function from Preoperative CT Scans
stories.Summary:
A team of researchers has developed a hybrid artificial intelligence model that can estimate how well a patient's lungs will work after surgery, using only a routine preoperative CT scan. The study, published in European Radiology Experimental in 2026 and reported by bioengineer.org on November 8, 2026, was led by Wang, Sun, Ma and Li. The model combines transfer-learned deep neural representations with elastic net regression to predict forced vital capacity and forced expiratory volume in one second, without requiring preoperative lung function tests or detailed surgical planning. The researchers say it is aimed at patients with pulmonary nodules who may undergo lobectomy, segmentectomy or wedge resection.

The motivation is that lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide, and rising detection of nodules has increased the number of thoracic operations. Surgeons must weigh removing enough tissue to treat the disease against preserving functioning lung. The traditional segment-counting method works only for anatomical segmentectomies and lobectomies, not wedge resections, and it depends on baseline spirometry while often overestimating functional loss. The study used data from 105 surgical patients at Huadong Hospital affiliated to Fudan University, drawn from 7,494 screened between October 2014 and October 2023, with 61 women and 44 men averaging 65.4 years old, and a separate external cohort of 31 patients from Heilongjiang Provincial Hospital treated between January 2017 and January 2023. In external testing, the hybrid model outperformed four alternative approaches and the segment-counting method, with a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.707 for forced vital capacity and 0.729 for forced expiratory volume in one second.

The authors, Wang, Sun, Ma and Li, presented the approach as an automated tool to support individualized decisions in common thoracic resections, though they were careful to describe its limits. Their own summary, paraphrased here, is that the study was retrospective, that the sample was modest because postoperative spirometry is not routinely performed, and that the clinical inputs were limited to six basic parameters. They concluded that larger prospective multicenter studies with standardized postoperative testing will be needed before the tool can be used in surgical practice. The article does not report any regulatory review or clinical rollout, so the model currently remains a research finding.

Articles.Title: Hybrid AI Model Predicts Postoperative Lung Function from Preoperative CT Scans

stories.Headline: Fire hawks inspire encryption and AI pairing to guard healthcare cloud data
stories.Summary:
Researchers have published a two-layer security system for healthcare cloud data that combines an encryption scheme with a machine-learning screen for access requests. The framework, called OFHXOR-PSL, appeared as an open-access paper in Discover Computing and was tested on two Internet of Health Things datasets. It reported a detection accuracy of 95.68 percent and a security level of 98.56 percent, with an attack level of 4 percent. The work is described in an article dated November 8, 2026, which was reported by Scienmag.

The system addresses a concern that hospitals face as they store electronic medical records on third-party cloud infrastructure. The authors say that common tools such as AES, RSA, and ECC, along with standard classifiers, can be computationally inefficient and weak at spotting threats. Their approach treats encryption and intrusion detection as one jointly designed pipeline instead of two separate tasks. The encryption layer uses XOR with a key chosen by the Fire Hawks Optimizer, a method modeled on birds of prey, and each session gets its own key. The paper reports an average key entropy of 7.94 bits per byte, close to the theoretical maximum of 8.

The second layer screens every request to reach stored records. A gateway extracts features such as IP address, query pattern, access frequency, session duration, and a geolocation anomaly score, then passes them to an ensemble of three classifiers. If uncertainty exceeds a threshold of 0.45, the request is blocked as suspicious. The authors also say the detection module keeps learning after a malicious classification, which they describe as a way to handle new attacks. The experiments used the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 and ECU-IoHT datasets, and the proposed ensemble outperformed artificial neural network, K-nearest neighbors, and support vector machine baselines.

The authors state that the research was carried out by A. CG, A. C, and R. Neerukonda, and they acknowledge several open questions. They note that key distribution assumes a pre-established secure channel such as TLS 1.3, and that user authentication and trust management were not tested experimentally. They also say that ciphertext integrity would need separate protection, for example with an HMAC, because XOR offers no diffusion. Future plans include post-quantum key encapsulation based on CRYSTALS-Kyber, federated learning, and validation on more datasets. The source code is openly available on GitHub under an MIT licence.

Articles.Title: Fire hawks inspire encryption and AI pairing to guard healthcare cloud data

stories.Headline: Feeling AI in Fashion Retail: Mixed Effects on Employee Creativity
stories.Summary:
A study published in Fashion and Textiles on November 8, 2026, found that emotionally responsive artificial intelligence, often called "feeling AI," does not uniformly boost creativity among fashion retail employees. The researchers, led by Ishtehar Sharif Swazan, reported that the psychological effects depend on the context and on which AI features are involved. Some features raised employees' confidence in their creative work, while others produced anxiety that changed how they approached creative tasks. The authors stressed that this distinction matters for an industry that depends on human innovation and aesthetic judgment.

The study examined two capabilities of feeling AI, anthropomorphism and personalization, and how they shape creative self-efficacy and job replacement anxiety. Those psychological states in turn affect two forms of creativity: proactive creativity, which is self-initiated, and responsive creativity, which is prompted by outside demands. The researchers treated AI as a psychological stimulus rather than only a technical tool. The survey covered 302 professionals working in U.S. fashion retail across buying, merchandising, planning, forecasting, marketing, product development, and customer service. The sample was 55.6 percent female and 43.7 percent male, and most participants held a bachelor's degree and had four to six years of experience.

The researchers analyzed the data with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling, and the model explained 22 percent of the variance in creative self-efficacy and 14.1 percent in proactive creativity. The results showed that anthropomorphism significantly reduced creative self-efficacy while also significantly increasing job replacement anxiety. Personalization strongly boosted creative self-efficacy, though its hypothesized effect on reducing job replacement anxiety was not statistically significant. Creative self-efficacy predicted proactive creativity, and job replacement anxiety significantly increased responsive creativity without significantly reducing proactive creativity. Subgroup analyses found that personalization varied by job function, with planning and forecasting roles reporting more of it than customer service, while the other mechanisms were consistent across departments.

The study notes several limitations, including its cross-sectional design, which limits causal conclusions, and its U.S.-only sample, which may not generalize globally. Sales, marketing, and customer service staff were more heavily represented than design and merchandising professionals. For managers, the authors suggest favoring personalized, adaptive tools over highly human-like agents, investing in training that builds creative self-efficacy, and communicating openly about how work is changing. The research adds to the literature on human-AI collaboration by focusing on psychological effects rather than operational utility. The authors call for future work to test the model across cultural contexts and to study the effects of AI integration over time.

Articles.Title: Feeling AI in Fashion Retail: Mixed Effects on Employee Creativity

stories.Headline: Analog Devices Completes Acquisition Of Alif Semiconductor To Expand Edge AI And Intelligent Computing Capabilities
stories.Summary:
Analog Devices, a global semiconductor company focused on sensing, signal processing, power management, and connectivity, has completed its acquisition of Alif Semiconductor. The deal was reported on November 7, 2026. Analog Devices says the transaction expands its capabilities in AI-native microcontrollers and embedded computing. The acquisition brings together Analog Devices' existing portfolio with Alif's microcontroller and fusion processor technologies.

Alif builds processing solutions that bring artificial intelligence directly into embedded devices, so those systems can process information and make some decisions locally. The articles say this matters most for applications that need low power consumption, short response times, strong security, and dependable performance. Analog Devices expects the combination to strengthen its position in intelligent edge computing, where chips interpret sensor data and respond to real-world conditions. Its existing products convert physical signals into digital information, while Alif's processors add AI computing that can run closer to the data source. The articles note that this can reduce reliance on remote cloud infrastructure in some settings.

Potential uses named in the coverage include industrial equipment that detects operating conditions, robotic systems that interpret sensor input, and healthcare devices that analyze data locally. The technologies may also serve energy infrastructure, defense electronics, and wearable devices. Analog Devices, whose CEO and chair is Vincent Roche, describes these capabilities as an extension of its platform at the intersection of physical and digital technologies. In his statement, Roche welcomed the Alif team and said the combined technologies can help systems understand real-world signals and act locally within demanding constraints. The company said the deal should widen its addressable markets and create more chances to combine sensing, connectivity, processing, and software in customer solutions.

Analog Devices reported more than $11 billion in revenue for fiscal 2025 and serves customers across industrial, automotive, communications, healthcare, and energy markets. The company has pointed to growing demand for AI outside traditional data centers, particularly in devices that interpret physical information. The articles do not state the purchase price or give details on how the companies will integrate their operations. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Analog Devices Completes Acquisition Of Alif Semiconductor To Expand Edge AI And Intelligent Computing Capabilities

stories.Headline: While smartphone screens are growing around foldable phones and artificial intelligence (AI) is crea..
stories.Summary:
Global tablet shipments fell to their lowest level in three years in the third quarter of this year, according to market research firm Omdia, which reported on the 7th. Shipments reached 32 million units, down 23 percent from the same period last year, and marked the second straight quarter of double-digit declines after a 10 percent drop in the previous quarter. The decline was especially steep in the Middle East, China and Western Europe. Even Apple, the market leader, could not avoid the slump, as its shipments fell 28 percent and its market share slipped to 36 percent.

Samsung Electronics stayed in second place with 5.4 million units, though its shipments dropped 22 percent and its share stood at 16.9 percent. Xiaomi fell 11 percent to 2.3 million units but edged its market share up to 7.3 percent on stronger sales in Latin America. Huawei's shipments plunged 43 percent to 1.8 million units. Major makers, including Samsung with its Galaxy Tab S12 series, Apple with an OLED iPad mini, and Xiaomi with its Pad 9 series, released new models in the second half of the year, yet none of them changed the market mood.

Omdia pointed to supply constraints and a lack of clear differentiation in new products as the main causes of weakening demand. Analysts said manufacturers struggle to offer specification upgrades that stand out from earlier models, since tablets handle video, web browsing and writing well enough even on devices released years ago. Foldable phones with larger screens are absorbing some tablet uses, while AI is creating replacement demand for PCs, including "AIPC" machines and local AI on compact desktops. Analysts also noted that AI features on tablets have not offered a decisive reason to buy a new device, and Omdia's research manager Himani Muka said tighter supply conditions next year could push tablets further down manufacturers' priorities, making a meaningful recovery difficult until 2028.

Articles.Title: While smartphone screens are growing around foldable phones and artificial intelligence (AI) is crea..

stories.Headline: Large Wall Street hedge funds, which lost money as artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks plung..
stories.Summary:
Large Wall Street hedge funds that lost money as AI-related stocks plunged after the Democratic Party's landslide victory in the U.S. midterm elections have started cutting their investment positions and shrinking their size. The Wall Street Journal reported on November 6 (local time) that Morgan Stanley's active reduction of stock-selective hedge fund positions last month reached its highest level in more than a decade. According to the report, these funds have cut their exposure to the stock market by about 9% since June.
